entry.title: μ-Bench: A Benchmark for Multi-User Task Completion by Shared Voice Agents
entry.summary: μ-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces μ-Bench, a benchmark for testing whether voice agents in shared spaces can complete tasks for several users at once while respecting each user's permissions and privacy. Simulated participants act from separate profiles of goals, knowledge, and permissions, and they respond to the agent's speech and tool results. The benchmark covers 20 domains and 800 cases, and it measures joint task success along with attribution, threading, and coordination diagnostics.

entry.title: CADENCE: a sensor-grounded collaborative Gaussian SLAM for building indoor maps with several phones
entry.summary: CADENCE: Sensor-GroundedWorld-Consistent Gaussian SLAM for Collaborative Mobile Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 26, 2026CADENCE is a collaborative indoor mapping system in which several phones build a shared 3D Gaussian map. It finds candidate matches between devices using a regional memory, then checks them geometrically before letting peer observations update the map. On eight Matterport3D houses, the regional memory reached an AUROC of 0.95 to 0.97, and soft confidence weighting reduced rendering quality loss under degradations. On twelve iPhone scans, tracking achieved a mean absolute trajectory error of 6.98 cm.

entry.title: Reducing Hallucinations in ESC Cardiology Guideline Medical QA: Evaluation and Retrieval Tuning
entry.summary: Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical Question Answering on ESC Cardiology Guidelines: Evaluation and Retrieval Optimization arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies hallucinations in medical question answering by large language models, using 160 questions built on four ESC cardiology guidelines. It evaluates a claim-level verify-and-revise pipeline against human judgement. Only 44.7% to 50.6% of flagged claims were true hallucinations, and verifier reliability was identified as the limiting factor. The final genuine-error rate was 1.7% of answers.

entry.title: MedSkill-E²: Testing and Improving Medical AI Agents' Use of Skills
entry.summary: MedSkill-E²: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces MedSkill-E², a framework for evaluating and improving how medical AI agents use skills. The authors build EBU-Bench, a benchmark covering 12 medically relevant task groups, and find that agents often fail to apply a skill's rules during autonomous execution, a problem they call Enable But Underuse (EBU). They also propose EBU-Evolve, which turns execution feedback into revised, reusable skill instructions that improve autonomous skill use across models and harnesses.

entry.title: Reliable user simulators for complex multi-step workflows
entry.summary: Reliable User Simulation in Complex Multi-Step Workflows arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies whether LLM-based user simulators stay faithful to their goals in complex, multi-step workflows used to test conversational assistants. The authors build a benchmark of 500 workflows represented with Hierarchical Task Networks and find that simulator fidelity drops sharply as complexity rises, with goal drift causing most failures. They propose ReUST, a prompting method that tracks user state across dialogue turns, which improves goal success for mid-sized and large models and reduces sensitivity to the assistant's response style.

entry.title: Where to Approximate: Speeding Up Looped Multi-View 3D Reconstruction
entry.summary: Where to Approximate: Understanding and Accelerating Looped Multi-View Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how approximating a shared transformer block in looped multi-view reconstruction affects later refinement steps and the final output. Using paired interventions on Déjà View and stacked reconstruction transformers, the authors propose reducing spatial resolution early, pooling keys and values, and interleaving attention-output reuse with full attention, adapted through lightweight self-distillation. Across five benchmarks, the balanced configuration runs 1.63 times faster than the official 16-step Déjà View model, with a 1.86-point drop in average pose AUC@3°.

entry.title: A complexity result showing tokenisation is not in APX
entry.summary: Tokenisation is not in APX arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper proves that, unless P=NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can find a tokeniser whose objective is within any constant factor of the optimum, so tokenisation is not in the APX class. The proof covers direct and bottom-up tokenisation, both compression and unigram log-likelihood objectives, and binary or larger alphabets. It further shows that direct tokenisation is APX-hard even over unary alphabets, so no polynomial-time approximation scheme exists. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove tokenisation admits no constant-factor polynomial-time approximation unless P=NP, and show APX-hardness for direct tokenisation.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer: a Transformer that reuses layers in loops more efficiently
entry.summary: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes the Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), which reuses shared layers across loops and selectively reads keys and values as memory between loops to balance expressivity and efficiency. It also introduces U-MoLT, a U-shaped variant that separates memory construction from prediction and skips unused decoder traversals. Experiments include 400B-token pretraining compared with OLMo3 and continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, reporting better token efficiency and benchmark results. Code is publicly available. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose MoLT, using KV as cross-loop memory, reporting gains over OLMo3 in 400B-token pretraining and Qwen3.5 continued pretraining; code is released.

entry.title: Cairn: Frozen Robot Models Steered by Learned 3D Object Paths
entry.summary: Cairn: Object-Centric 3D Trajectory Priors for Steering Frozen VLAs arXiv · Nov 26, 2026Vision-language-action models often fail when objects are moved or obstacles appear, because they rely on training layouts. This paper introduces Cairn, which keeps the model frozen and guides it at test time along learned 3D trajectories of the held object, generated from scene point clouds, the object's grasp pose, and the instruction. Across 1,941 held-out LIBERO scenes, the success rate of a frozen π0.5 rises from 24.5% to 95.1%. It also transfers to a real Franka robot, where it avoids an obstacle and reaches a placement at the limit of the arm's reach. ★★★★ Notable: The authors steer a frozen VLA at test time with a learned object-centric 3D trajectory prior, reporting large success gains on 1,941 LIBERO scenes and a real Franka arm.

entry.title: Estimating object material from drop videos, trained in simulation
entry.summary: What a Drop Reveals: Sim-to-Real Material Estimation for Deformable Objects from Video arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper estimates a deformable object's density-normalized stiffness E/ρ and, when impact causes plastic deformation, its yield stress σY/ρ from one real video of the object dropping. The predictor is trained only on simulated data. The authors find that synthetic validation ranks geometric inputs wrongly: 3D-lifted tracklets are most accurate in simulation but least accurate on real drops, while short 2D optical-flow tracklets transfer best. Their predictor, PhysReader, is closer to reference materials than other inputs and baselines on the real-object benchmark PhysReader-Real. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show simulation validation misranks geometric inputs, and propose PhysReader, trained in simulation, evaluated on their PhysReader-Real dataset against reference materials.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Offline Reinforcement Learning Under Recursive Entropic Risk
entry.summary: Provably Efficient Offline Discounted Reinforcement Learning under Recursive Entropic Risk arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies risk-sensitive reinforcement learning in discounted infinite-horizon Markov decision processes, using recursive entropic risk measures with parameter β≠0. It covers both risk-averse (β>0) and risk-seeking (β<0) settings in the offline setting, where a fixed dataset is used to learn a near-optimal policy. The authors propose a model-based algorithm, ERM-VI-LCB, and derive a PAC-type sample complexity bound, along with a matching lower bound showing exponential dependence on |β|/(1-γ) is unavoidable in the worst case. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give sample complexity upper and lower bounds for offline RL under recursive entropic risk, covering both risk-averse and risk-seeking settings.

entry.title: Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark: Testing whether language models know early-grade literacy basics
entry.summary: The Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark: Do Language Models Know the Foundations of Early-Grade Literacy? arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces the Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark, a largely automated pipeline that builds a vetted question set from curriculum documents, teacher guides and pupil books, organised by nine linguistic domains and seven grade levels. It was applied to Kiswahili (135 items) and English (137 items), evaluating 121 and 119 models. Frontier models exceed 90% accuracy in both languages, but smaller and cheaper models perform much worse, especially in Kiswahili. The authors release a sample of items, pipeline prompts, code, and a public leaderboard. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a literacy-grounded linguistic benchmark and report 121 and 119 models on Kiswahili and English, with small models markedly weaker in Kiswahili.

entry.title: Guidance as Variance Matching: A Rule for Choosing Diffusion Guidance Scales
entry.summary: Guidance as Variance Matching arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how guidance improves diffusion models, which steers predictions away from a weaker reference prediction to raise sample quality. The authors find that at practical scales guidance worsens the posterior-mean prediction while samples improve. They introduce variance-matched guidance, a closed-form rule that chooses the guidance scale by matching the variance of guided predictions to that of the data, and it reproduces the hand-picked scales of eleven widely used models. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a closed-form variance-matching rule that recovers hand-picked guidance scales of eleven models without tuning, and offer a new mechanism interpretation.

entry.title: CIRKDV2: Cross-image relational knowledge distillation with context modeling for efficient segmentation
entry.summary: CIRKDV2: Cross-Image Relational Knowledge Distillation with Contextual Modeling for Efficient Semantic Segmentation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes CIRKDV2, a knowledge distillation method for semantic segmentation that lets a small student network mimic a large teacher's structured semantic relations. Unlike methods that use only one image at a time, it transfers pixel-to-pixel, pixel-to-region, and channel-to-channel relations modeled across global images in the dataset. It also uses context aggregation to enrich student pixel features, reducing the semantic gap with the teacher. Experiments on Cityscapes, ADE20K, Pascal VOC, and COCO-Stuff-164K show it outperforms prior segmentation distillation methods across various architectures. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend relational distillation across images with contextual feature distillation, reporting gains over prior methods on four segmentation datasets.

entry.title: RevFlow: Generating Images by Reversing a Frozen Encoder's Layers
entry.summary: Generation as Reverse Encoding arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces RevFlow, which treats generation as reverse encoding by using the intermediate representations of a frozen encoder as successive generative targets. It first generates deep semantic representations, then shallow ones that keep appearance and spatial detail, before decoding to pixels. A unified HyC-DiT model with a shared DiT backbone and stage-specific condition injection learns these transitions. On ImageNet 256×256, the authors report FID scores of 1.96 (690M) and 1.74 (1.55B) after 5 training epochs.. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose staged reverse generation through frozen encoder intermediate representations, with a shared DiT backbone, reporting ImageNet 256 FID results.

entry.title: TASK Memory: Text Memory Plus Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing to Reduce Memory Hallucination
entry.summary: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how LLM agents hallucinate about external memory even when the correct memory is retrieved, identifying memory-ignoring, memory-misapplying, and version-confusion failures. It proposes TASK memory, which pairs a text note with activation steering and knowledge editing that share one in-model address, using steering vectors to decide per query whether the model adopts the memory. On frozen models, the authors report large reductions in memory-ignoring and neighbour-misuse hallucinations, along with gains over BM25 RAG and multi-hop accuracy on MQuAKE. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine text memory with activation steering and removable knowledge editing sharing one in-model address, reporting reduced memory hallucination across five open models and multiple datas

entry.title: From NP-hard to exactly solvable via sample abundance: a theory paper on noisy parity fitting
entry.summary: From NP-Hardness to Exact Tractability Through Sample Abundance arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper studies noisy parity fitting, a worst-case NP-hard optimization problem. It shows that additional independent observations can make exact optimization tractable without changing the objective or feasible set. The authors give the number of extra readings needed for exact optimization with high probability, along with the computational cost. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show noisy parity fitting becomes exactly solvable with enough random samples, giving a tight sample-complexity order under a uniform rank-one sign tensor model.

entry.title: Spec2Weights: Proving That Networks a Language Model Writes from a Specification Are Exact
entry.summary: Spec2Weights: Certifying Networks that a Language Model Writes from a Specification arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper studies whether a language model can write the weights of small neural networks directly from a plain-language specification, without data or gradient training. It introduces methods to prove such networks exact under float32 arithmetic, using enumeration, dynamic programming, SMT proofs and induction. The authors certify 12 of 15 written networks on stated input domains. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report certifying float32 exactness over stated input domains for 12 of 15 LM-written networks and 25 of 30 new specifications, a novel verification angle.

entry.title: ShowNow: Fast-Responding Interactive Video Generation via Speculative Streaming
entry.summary: ShowNow: Fine-Grained Speculative Streaming for Responsive World Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces ShowNow, a framework for interactive world models that generates video continuously while responding to user actions. It uses computation during playback to prepare action-conditioned future frames before input arrives, with single-latent commitment enabling frequent decisions. In ViZDoom, the full deployment reduces median input-to-display latency from 620 ms to 208 ms compared with the SolarWM-FT baseline. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prepare multiple action-conditioned futures during playback to cut input latency in interactive world models, reporting ViZDoom median latency falling from 620 to 208 ms.

entry.title: RoboEvo²: Robots improving themselves by co-evolving their policies and control harnesses
entry.summary: RoboEvo²: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper proposes RoboEvo², a framework in which a robot's control policy and its harness (coding agent and control APIs) evolve together recursively, without extra human demonstrations. Policy failures guide the coding agent to search for alternative solutions, which are consolidated into reusable skills, while verified trajectories train the policy. On LIBERO-PRO, standalone success rises from 11.0% to 84.1% and hybrid success from 30.4% to 90.5%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose recursive harness-policy co-evolution with counterfactual preference distillation, reporting large success gains on LIBERO-PRO and RoboTwin.

entry.title: VisualMontage: Using Authentic Image Sequences to Manipulate Vision-Language Agents' Beliefs
entry.summary: VisualMontage: Manipulating the Beliefs of Vision-Language Agents with Authentic Image Sequences arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how vision-language model agents that interpret social-media posts can be misled by coordinated posts combining real images with accurate-looking captions. The authors build a benchmark of 544 target cases and 33.2K candidate images across eight domains. They also propose VisualMontage, a multi-agent framework that simulates such attacks. Experiments across 12 models show the attacks transfer between models, with mean success rates of 61.93% for proprietary and 68.71% for open-weight models. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce visual cognitive collusion, using authentic image sequences to steer vision-language agents; reported experiments span 544 cases and 12 models.

entry.title: Long-range robot planning using graph anchors in latent world models
entry.summary: Long-Horizon Planning with Latent World Models via Graph Anchors arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper argues that latent world model planners judge progress by latent distance to the goal, which loses directional signal far from the goal and overweights the robot arm over the manipulated object during contact. The authors propose Graph Anchors, a training-free planner that builds a sparse graph over training frames and aims each step at a node a few moves ahead on the shortest path to the goal. On goals up to 400 steps away, success rose from 13% to 85% on PointMaze-Medium, from 8% to 87% on PointMaze-Large, and from 5% to 71% on Push-T. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a training-free planner aiming at nearby graph nodes instead of distant goals, and report large success gains on PointMaze and Push-T.

entry.title: Efficient Data Fusion in Distributionally Robust Optimization
entry.summary: Efficient Data Fusion in Distributionally Robust Optimization arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how to combine fragmented evidence, such as samples from different populations or privacy-protected summary statistics, for decision-making under uncertainty. It uses distributionally robust optimization, building one ambiguity set per source and hedging against all distributions in their intersection. The authors derive affine-rule upper bounds that decompose across ambiguity sets and are exact for quadratic losses over Wasserstein balls around Gaussian references. Experiments in portfolio, newsvendor, and classification settings show the approximation stays close to the exact value where computable, scales better, and outperforms aggregation-based benchmarks out-of-sample. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reformulate multi-source distributionally robust optimization via functional Lagrange multipliers, give decomposable affine upper bounds, and report near-exact values and out-of-sample gai

entry.title: Who Wears the Camera? Locating Camera Wearers Across Views Beyond Humans
entry.summary: Who Is Ego? Scaling Cross-View Camera Wearer Identification and Segmentation beyond Humans arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper addresses identifying who or what wears a first-person camera, using a synchronized third-person image, for wearers including robots, vehicles, animals and drones. It introduces FindEgo-1M, a dataset of 1.16M real and simulated ego-exo image pairs. The proposed EgoRay-ZS method is training-free, and the full EgoRay model reports higher accuracy and speed than the compared baselines. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use the epipole geometry to identify camera wearers across views, reusing a frozen 3D reconstruction model training-free, and report gains on a new large dataset.

entry.title: Convergence of second-order training methods for physics-informed neural networks as network width grows
entry.summary: Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper analyzes the convergence of regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton methods for training physics-informed neural networks that solve partial differential equations. As the number of hidden units goes to infinity, training converges in probability to a deterministic limit equation involving a Newton neural tangent kernel operator. The authors prove that the PDE residual vanishes during training and that the network converges to the PDE solution under mild assumptions. They also show that a sufficiently small regularization parameter makes the residual's projections onto leading eigenfunctions decay exponentially, so the parameter acts as a spectral filter. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a convergence analysis for regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton training of PINNs in the overparameterized limit, with explicit rates and a spectral-filter interpretation.

entry.title: Decision-focused learning for multistage stochastic planning, applied to power grid repair scheduling
entry.summary: Decision-Focused Learning for Multistage Stochastic Programs, with Application to Power Network Repair Scheduling arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a decision-focused learning framework for multistage stochastic programs with discrete decisions, where a neural network predicts scores for the part of the decision that drives state transitions. The network is trained on labels from offline single-scenario problems using the Fenchel-Young loss with perturbed optimizers. Applied to repairing failed components in a 5-bus and an IEEE 14-bus power network, with and without a per-stage repair budget, the method is the cheapest policy under a binding budget, 14% to 23% below the next-best policy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend decision-focused learning to multistage stochastic programs, training a network with Fenchel-Young loss and applying it to power network repair scheduling under budget constraints.

entry.title: Single-database rewards can be gamed; counterfactual execution aims to make text-to-SQL RL trustworthy
entry.summary: Single-Database Rewards Are Hackable: Counterfactual Execution for Trustworthy Text-to-SQL RL arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper argues that reinforcement learning rewards for text-to-SQL agents, which check query results on a single database, can be satisfied by wrong queries that match by luck when the data lack revealing rows. The authors propose a counterfactual-database reward that also runs the final query on several hidden, code-generated database copies, paying only if all results match (strict form) or by the share matched (mean form). On 1,302 synthetic audit questions, the strict form substantially reduces buggy queries receiving full reward and reward hacks, without rejecting any of 2,847 correct queries. ★★★★ Notable: The authors add hidden counterfactual database copies to verify SQL rewards and curb reward hacking. They report results on 1,302 synthetic audit questions and three-seed GRPO comparisons.

entry.title: Navigent: A geometry-grounded agent framework for vision-language navigation
entry.summary: Navigent: A Geometry-Grounded Agentic Framework for Vision Language Navigation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents Navigent, an agentic framework for vision-and-language navigation built on a frozen multimodal large language model. Its Geometry-Grounded Execution Critic checks whether measured movement matches commanded actions and whether tracked visual landmarks align with world coordinates, triggering reobservation, local adjustment, or recovery when discrepancies appear. An offline procedure refines prompts and critic logic from successful and failed trajectories without changing model weights. Navigent reports 84.0% and 86.0% success rates on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE validation-unseen splits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors add geometry-based consistency checks to a frozen MLLM navigator, reporting high SR and SPL on R2R-CE and RxR-CE unseen validation splits.

entry.title: Whether models predict drug targets or already know the answer
entry.summary: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper tests whether language models can forecast the first clinical trial of a drug target for a disease, using a dated biomedical knowledge graph rebuilt at the end of each year from 2020. Six open models were evaluated with and without the graph, predicting trials in the following year. Without retrieval, the models performed about as well as a simple past-trial count baseline, and pre-decision evidence added little. The newest graph lifted most models above that baseline, but its paths often contained the post-decision trial itself. The authors recommend dating both features and labels in target prioritisation evaluations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors recast target-disease hypotheses as dated first-trial events, test temporal forecasting, and report that graph paths often leak the outcome.

entry.title: SOLO: Sample-faithful, detectable LLM watermarking for repeated sampling
entry.summary: SOLO: Towards Sample-Faithful and Detectable LLM Watermarking under Repeated Sampling via Content-Anchored Single-Owner Contexts arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper shows that standard distortion-free watermarks for language models make multiple responses to the same prompt interfere with each other, because shared answer templates cause their watermark contexts to collide. The authors propose SOLO, which keeps a request-level context history but anchors keyed contexts on content chosen by min-hash, so sibling responses rarely compete and random edits stay local. Experiments on five language models from three families and three benchmarks report that SOLO preserves self-consistency and uncertainty estimation and, at a 1% false positive rate, detects more responses than four-token key pools on most tasks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose content-anchored single-owner contexts for repeated sampling watermarks, evaluated on five models and three benchmarks against key pools and context history.

entry.title: Detectable by Design: Learning a Continuous 3D Saliency Field
entry.summary: Detectable by Design: Learning a Continuous 3D Saliency Field from 2D Detector Responses arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper defines 3D saliency as image detectability, meaning how strongly a 2D interest-point detector responds to a surface point across all views where it is visible. The authors propose DetField, a continuous field that takes a point cloud as input and predicts detectability at any 3D location, using multi-scale curvature invariants in its decoder. In a localization benchmark isolating 3D point selection, DetField outperforms Harris-3D and five learned keypoint methods on objects and real indoor scenes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors define 3D saliency as 2D detector response and learn a continuous field, reporting gains over Harris-3D and learned keypoint methods on localization benchmarks.

entry.title: Improving speculative drafting with hidden state mixing and gradient detach
entry.summary: Improving Tail-Augmented Speculative Drafting with Hidden State Mixing and Gradient Detach arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper addresses a training-inference mismatch in multi-token prediction and EAGLE-style drafters used for speculative decoding. It proposes two training-only methods, Hidden State Mixing (HSM) and Hidden State Gradient Detach (HSGD), which add no inference cost. HSGD gives the highest acceptance rates at early draft positions, while HSM performs best later in the draft. Across several Nemotron models and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, HSM improves mean acceptance length by up to 52.2% over co-trained MTP. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose training-only hidden state mixing and gradient detach to reduce drafter train-inference mismatch, reporting acceptance length gains across several models versus EAGLE-3's TTT.

entry.title: Accelerated multiobjective sampling over probability measures via Hilbert-space lifting
entry.summary: Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods for Multiobjective Optimization over Probability Measures via Hilbert-Space Lifting arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper treats finding one distribution that balances several targets as Pareto multiobjective optimization of KL divergences over probability measures. It proposes multiobjective Wasserstein proximal gradient (MWPG) and its accelerated version MWAPG, which lift measures to pushforwards of a base measure by maps in a Hilbert space, yielding a constrained composite problem over transport maps. The authors prove discrete-time convergence rates, including O(1/k^2) for convex smooth potentials and linear rates under strong convexity. Experiments report that MWAPG needs far fewer iterations than MWPG and matches or beats A-MWGraD in Bayesian multi-task learning. ★★★★ Notable: The authors lift measures to Hilbert-space maps, yielding accelerated proximal methods with O(1/k^2) and linear discrete-time rates, tested on Bayesian multi-task learning.

entry.title: End-to-end image-goal navigation for agile quadrotors using recurrent state distillation
entry.summary: End-to-End Image-Goal Navigation for Agile Quadrotors via Recurrent State Distillation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents a policy that navigates a quadrotor in unseen 3D environments toward a goal photograph by directly commanding thrust and angular rates, without state estimation or a separate velocity controller. The recurrent vision-based policy is trained through a four-stage pipeline combining geometric and motion supervision, privileged-teacher distillation, and end-to-end reinforcement learning fine-tuning. It achieves an 82.3% success rate over 1000 held-out flights, with a mean terminal position error of 0.10 m for successful flights. Deployed zero-shot on a real quadrotor, it reaches an 84% success rate over 25 trials in an unseen indoor environment. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first image-goal policy commanding thrust and rates on quadrotors in unseen 3D settings, reporting 82.3% success over 1000 flights and 84% real-robot trials.

entry.title: JHealthBench-L: Clinician-Reviewed Japanese Localization of HealthBench for Medical LLM Evaluation
entry.summary: JHealthBench-L: Clinician-Reviewed Localization of HealthBench for Rubric-Based Medical LLM Evaluation in Japan arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents JHealthBench-L, a Japan-localized version of the HealthBench benchmark for evaluating large language models on open-ended health consultations. It contains 79 patient-facing consultations and 1,022 physician-style criteria, drafted with LLMs and then selected, revised, and independently reviewed by physicians. The authors compare it with a machine-translated baseline across 18 LLMs and report that translation alone keeps coarse model rankings but changes verdicts on 17.7% of modified criteria. ★★★★ Notable: The authors localize HealthBench rubrics for Japan with physician review and show machine translation masks item-level errors, reporting results across 18 LLMs.

entry.title: PatternMiner: An AI System That Combines LLM Agents and Small Models to Discover Math Theorems
entry.summary: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces PatternMiner, a system in which an LLM agent generates mathematical datasets, trains small machine learning models on them, and uses interpretability techniques to extract patterns and formulate conjectures. The agent then searches for counterexamples with mathematical software and refines conjectures iteratively, attempting proofs along the way. Applied to five positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics, the system proves several new theorems, including results on Schubert positivity and projection, a character-row evaluation formula, a restricted Kazhdan–Lusztig combinatorial invariance conjecture, and Schur positivity for a family of immanant coefficients. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine LLM agents with interpretable small models for open-ended conjecture discovery, reporting new theorems on positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics.

entry.title: BReD: Block Replay Dithering to Stabilize Low-Bit EMA Optimizer States
entry.summary: BReD: Block Replay Dithering for Stable Low-Bit EMA Optimizer States arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper shows that storing optimizer states in low-bit form is unstable because they are repeatedly dequantized, updated, and requantized each training step. For states updated by exponential moving averages, quantization errors accumulate recursively, especially when the decay factor is close to 1. The authors propose BReD, which adapts subtractive dithering using deterministic seed replay and block-wise shared dither values to reduce rounding bias and control variance. Experiments report that 4-bit BReD closely matches full-precision optimizer training across the evaluated pretraining and fine-tuning settings, and 3-bit BReD also converges stably in those settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors adapt subtractive dithering to optimizer-state quantization using seed replay and block-shared dither, reporting PPL and downstream results across 120M to 7B models.

entry.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Teaching Robot World Models to Predict Manipulation Failures
entry.summary: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper addresses how robot world models fail to predict outcomes when grasps go wrong, such as objects being pushed, tilted, or slipping. The authors build Reforge, a dataset of 62k simulated trajectories with perturbed grasps and ground-truth object pose and contact information. They propose WorldReforge, which adds two training signals, Interaction Alignment and Surface Correspondence, without extra inference cost. The method reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall, and it also improves reconstruction on DROID and real failure videos. ★★★★ Notable: The authors train robot world models on simulated failure trajectories with ground truth, adding interaction alignment and surface correspondence signals. They report 28.2% lower object trajectory err

entry.title: On the Learnability of Model Reprogramming: Reachability and Relabeling View
entry.summary: On the Learnability of Model Reprogramming: A Reachability and Relabeling Perspective arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how many target samples model reprogramming needs, where a frozen source model is adapted via a learnable input transformation and output mapping. It factorizes the wrapper hypothesis class complexity into a reachability term over source-label patterns and a conditional relabeling term, yielding an agnostic PAC estimation bound matched by a lower bound. It also decomposes the approximation error into source-label information loss and output-mapping restriction, with an upper bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors decompose wrapper sample complexity into reachability and relabeling terms, reporting an agnostic PAC bound matched by a lower bound and an exact approximation-error decomposition.

entry.title: Testing whether driving models truly understand roads they have not seen
entry.summary: Off the Driven Path: Transferable Road Understanding in Driving VLAs arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces Road-KSU, a framework that turns HD maps and actor annotations into road-centric scene graphs for question answering and trajectory compliance evaluation. On NAVSIM, nearly all test samples lie close to training samples, and planner scores on turns rise with the number of training drives through the same location, suggesting memorized road geometry. Experiments on geographically disjoint splits show action performance drops most on unfamiliar turns, and the authors conclude that geographic diversity is key to transferable road knowledge. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce Road-KSU and geographically disjoint splits, reporting on NAVSIM that planners rely on memorized road geometry and that place diversity drives transferable road knowledge.

entry.title: AnyCam: Using an Anchor Object as the Camera for Video Generation
entry.summary: AnyCam: Anything Can Represent Camera for Video Generation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026AnyCam proposes representing the camera with an anchor object in the scene, reconstructing it in 3D and rendering it along a target trajectory as a camera signal. A video diffusion model uses this signal to transfer the source video's content and dynamics to the new viewpoint. The model can be distilled into AnyCam-AR, a streaming generator for on-the-fly camera control. Experiments reportedly show favorable results against camera-controlled video generation and 3D reconstruction methods.

entry.title: Tracking Any Point Using an Agent That Reasons Over Video
entry.summary: Tracking Any Point with Agentic Visual Reasoning arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper presents AgenTAP, a vision-language model agent that directly predicts point coordinates and visibility while actively inspecting videos to verify point identity and refine its predictions. Without correspondence-specific fine-tuning, it reportedly outperforms expert vision models in point localization and visibility prediction. The authors also use it to build EgoTAP-4D, a dataset of 3D point trajectories from long real-world egocentric videos.

entry.title: Adapting AI-native autoencoder communication systems to new channels via transfer learning
entry.summary: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies AI-native communications built on autoencoders, which jointly train transmitter and receiver encoder-decoder pairs. Models trained only on an AWGN channel perform poorly on Rayleigh fading with practical front-end impairments. The authors propose a low-latency transfer-learning method that starts from an AWGN-pretrained system and fine-tunes only a small subset of layers, selecting which layers to update through a budget-constrained optimization. Partial updates remove the mismatch-induced error floor and approach the bit error rate of fully retrained models, while reducing training time, operations, energy, and updated parameters.

entry.title: Improving video editing without new paired videos
entry.summary: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT), which uses an image editor to improve pretrained video editors and extend them to new tasks, trained only on single images with no architectural changes and no new videos. The video editor treats an image as a one-frame video, and at test time the learned capabilities apply to whole clips while preserving temporal consistency. The authors also extend the OpenVE-Bench benchmark into OpenVE++, adding four tasks: action changes, expression changes, body movements, and scene relighting. They report state-of-the-art results on both OpenVE-Bench and OpenVE++ across three video editors.

entry.title: LuxAvatar: Real-Time Relightable Head Avatars via Causal Neural Shading of 3D Intrinsic Proxies
entry.summary: LuxAvatar: Real-Time Relightable Head Avatars via Causal Neural Shading of 3D Intrinsic Proxies arXiv · Nov 26, 2026LuxAvatar is a feed-forward framework that animates and relights a head avatar in real time from a single portrait. It splits avatar synthesis into an animatable 3D intrinsic Gaussian proxy and a causal autoregressive neural shader that generates shading under target illumination through a conditional video diffusion process. The authors achieve streaming speed by distilling a multi-step bidirectional relighting teacher into a two-step causal shader, and fine-tune it on a hybrid relighting dataset of human heads. The paper reports better visual fidelity, motion control, and lighting accuracy than prior methods.

entry.title: MEMO: A Method for Per-Frame Mesh Reconstruction of Dynamic Scenes
entry.summary: A Mesh for Every Moment arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper presents MEMO (a Mesh for Every MOment), which reconstructs the geometry of full dynamic scenes captured by multiple synchronized cameras and extracts a mesh at every frame. Its core is a per-Gaussian motion model inspired by Gaussian processes, representing each Gaussian's position and rotation over time with temporal Gaussian kernels, plus a track-based initialization for large, fast motion. The method is evaluated on the new Blender-Moments benchmark and two real-world datasets, where it reports the most accurate geometry among state-of-the-art methods while staying competitive in novel-view synthesis and training time.

entry.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
entry.summary: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This study tests whether a generated helper image improves answers to visual questions. Models describe the helper they need, then answer using both the original and generated images. Across 13 vision-language model and generator pairs, generation lowered mean accuracy by 3.7 percentage points, with declines on nine of ten tasks.

entry.title: Choice of attack policies may mislead evaluations of AI monitors
entry.summary: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper uses an ex-production OpenAI monitor as a case study and finds that its measured false negative rate is highly sensitive to how attack policies are generated and how far they are optimised. Under one reinforcement learning method, the rate ranged from 0.5% to 20.8% across optimisation levels. The authors warn that evaluations using only basic attack methods can create false confidence, so interpreting results as evidence about deployment needs a separate justification of why the proxy attacks are informative.

entry.title: DynMF2: EM-based rigid motion factorization for monocular 4D scene reconstruction and motion segmentation
entry.summary: DynMF2: Rigid Motion Factorization by Expectation-Maximization for Monocular 4D Reconstruction and Motion Segmentation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper reconstructs dynamic scenes from a single casual video by modeling scene motion as a small set of rigid SE(3) trajectories, with each point following exactly one of them. The method factorizes motion directly from 3D point trajectories using Expectation-Maximization, without rendering or masks, and treats the background as the camera's motion. The authors report that it clearly outperforms mask-based baselines in view synthesis on iPhone and NVIDIA data and in 3D tracking on iPhone, and it segments moving parts of MOVi-F and iTACO scenes competitively despite not being trained for segmentation.

entry.title: A gene-informed benchmark measuring how well pathology AI models capture cell types
entry.summary: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces BioScore, a benchmark that assesses how well image encoders for pathology capture cell identities, using spatial transcriptomics from the same tissue as reference. A sparse autoencoder splits patch embeddings into sparse features that are clustered, and each cluster is checked against the expression of marker genes for 52 cell identities. Eight pathology foundation models and three natural-image models were scored, and every pathology model ranked above every natural-image model.

entry.title: High-fidelity image matting using pixel-space diffusion transformers
entry.summary: High-Fidelity Image Matting with Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents PixelMatte, a framework that adapts pretrained pixel-space diffusion transformers for image matting, avoiding the detail loss of latent diffusion models. It processes the input image, trimap, and noisy alpha matte as spatially aligned tokens and predicts alpha mattes in a single forward pass, with two lightweight calibration modules, LayerShift and High-Pass Refiner. Reported results show SAD and gradient errors reduced by 24-44% relative to RenderMatte on P3M-500-NP and AM-2K.

entry.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems: Mining Rejected Reasoning Traces to Supplement Training Data for LLMs
entry.summary: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes DART, a method for mining training data for large language models on hard math problems. It starts from a rejected reasoning trace, splits it into steps, ranks them by position-weighted uncertainty, and generates distinct alternative steps using reference-answer guidance and a meta-thought before completing the traces. On DeepMath-103K problems unsolved by greedy decoding, DART recovers 37% more problems than Monte Carlo sampling at a matched number of generated traces, with 30% lower cost per accepted trace. Post-training Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on DART-mined traces yields the highest point estimate in five of six evaluations across MATH-500 and AIME.

entry.title: LiveVAE: Efficient Streaming Video VAE Using Causal Window Attention
entry.summary: LiveVAE: Causal Window Attention Makes Efficient Streaming Video VAE arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper addresses the video VAE as a latency bottleneck in interactive video generation and editing, where prior methods mainly speed up decoding and rely on heavy convolutions or full-frame attention. By analyzing pretrained video VAEs, the authors find that encoding and decoding depend mostly on spatial and temporal neighbors. They propose LiveVAE, a streaming encoder and decoder built on causal window attention, which serves as a drop-in replacement for the original VAE. On MiniMax-H3, LiveVAE reports 5.2-6.2x faster encoding and 3.0-3.3x faster decoding with higher PSNR.

entry.title: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Memory for Long Video Generation
entry.summary: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper presents Agentic LongLive, an asynchronous memory system for real-time autoregressive long video generation. A memory agent on separate GPUs reads only revealed prompts and maintains text states and images for each person, object, and scene, which are prefilled into the generator so video generation does not wait for memory updates. On the new LongStory-Online benchmark, it improves persistent-state accuracy, protagonist identity, and revisited-place consistency over its base generator, at about 1% extra generation time.

entry.title: ProbFaS: Probabilistic Video Frame Selection for MLLMs via Multi-Fidelity Calibration
entry.summary: ProbFaS: Probabilistic Video Frame Selection for MLLMs via Multi-Fidelity Calibration arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes ProbFaS, a training- and label-free method for selecting key video frames so that multimodal large language models can process long videos more cheaply. It combines dense but biased image-text alignment scores with sparse but accurate MLLM yes/no judgments using co-kriging, a multi-fidelity Gaussian process, and then applies a temporal determinantal point process to pick relevance peaks while keeping temporal coverage. On Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench, ProbFaS achieves the highest accuracy among fourteen training-free selectors and uniform sampling in 13 of 15 settings.

entry.title: Using latent-space embeddings to improve ship detection and tracking in maritime monitoring
entry.summary: Enhancing Maritime Domain Awareness using Latent Space Representations arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper applies compressed latent-space embeddings from the TerraMind geospatial foundation model to detect, localise, and classify vessels in Sentinel-1 radar imagery, avoiding the need to process raw images. Vessel detection reaches a ROC-AUC of 0.95, and localisation has a median error of about 300 m for vessels longer than 100 m. AIS type-code classification reaches 62% accuracy for majority classes but correlates strongly with vessel length. The authors also release a dataset of about 2,000 Sentinel-1 images paired with AIS signals.

entry.title: Accurate, interpretable hybrid decision trees that combine feature and case-based splits
entry.summary: Interpretable and Accurate Hybrid Decision Trees with Selective Case-Based Splits arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes a hybrid decision tree architecture that allows both feature-based and case-based splits within one tree. It also introduces a selective case-based split, which searches for the most informative subset of features when a split is needed. Experiments on a range of tabular datasets reportedly show better performance than standard decision trees, performance comparable to ensemble methods, and shallower trees.

entry.title: FineDex: Linking Fine-Grained Human-Object Interaction Generation to Dexterous Humanoid Manipulation
entry.summary: FineDex: Bridging Fine-Grained Human-Object Interaction Generation to Dexterous Humanoid Manipulation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026FineDex is a framework that lets finger-level intent be both specified and carried out in robot manipulation. It generates coordinated human body, hand, and object motions that follow fine-grained instructions about hand selection, individual fingers, and contacts with articulated objects. The generated interactions serve as priors for an agent that learns feasible contact strategies through practice in a physics-based digital twin. Experiments report state-of-the-art interaction generation and controllability, improved dexterous manipulation success, and deployment on a real dexterous humanoid robot.

entry.title: Stranger Things: Object recognition when items appear without their usual companions
entry.summary: Stranger Things: When Objects Appear Without Their Typical Neighbors arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies typicality bias, where vision models predict objects based on which objects typically appear alongside them rather than on the objects' own visual features. The authors introduce a diagnostic framework and STRANGE-Bench, a photorealistic benchmark covering object pairs from typical to never-co-occurring. They find the bias across five model families and three recognition tasks, and propose Anchor-Atypicality Sampling, a data augmentation sampling rule that reduces the gap on COCO and the synthetic benchmark.

entry.title: Narrowing the performance gap in finding places from text descriptions
entry.summary: Towards Closing the Performance Gap in Cross-Modal Place Recognition arXiv · Nov 26, 2026Cross-modal place recognition locates a place by matching a natural language description against a database of geo-tagged reference images. The paper proposes CrossPlace, a two-stage framework: the first stage performs global retrieval with a DINOv2-B/14 visual backbone and a BGE-Large text encoder, and the second stage reranks top candidates with a lightweight token-level cross-attention module. The authors also evaluate city-scale settings and severe weather and illumination conditions. They report double-digit Recall@1 gains over prior cross-modal methods across all benchmarks.

entry.title: How much do coding agents over-edit, and why? A study of unneeded edits in repository-level patches
entry.summary: How Much Do Coding Agents Over-Edit, and Why? An Empirical Study of Unneeded Edits in Repository-Level Agent Patches arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper examines why coding agents produce larger patches than developers, a pattern often read as over-editing. It introduces Delta Residue Attribution (DRA), which traces each code unit of a final patch to the step that wrote it, reverts it, and reruns tests to judge whether it is needed. Applied to 7,660 resolved trajectories on SWE-bench Verified and DeepSWE, the study finds agent code is on average at least as necessary as developers' code, with about 11% of agent code units on SWE-bench Verified still unneeded.

entry.title: Shape-aware three-way merge for RDF knowledge graphs
entry.summary: Shape-Aware Three-Way Merge for RDF Knowledge Graphs: The schema defines the conflict: an implementation and evaluation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper describes a three-way merge method for RDF knowledge graphs in which SHACL shapes define when changes conflict. Unbounded predicates are combined by union, while contended slots, where both sides' changes cannot fit within the shape's cardinality bound, are referred to a person. The method is implemented in a production multi-agent store and compared with a reimplementation of Quit Store's Context Merge rule and six other strategies. On synthetic seeds it raised the same conflicts while asking far fewer questions, but it does not detect different names for the same entity.

entry.title: RePace: Speeding Up Robot Demonstrations to Train Faster Vision-Language-Action Policies
entry.summary: RePace: Reasoning about Demonstration Speedup for Faster Vision-Language-Action Policies arXiv · Nov 26, 2026Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can inherit the slow pace of human demonstrations, so speeding up demonstrations before fine-tuning can yield faster policies. This paper presents RePace, an offline reasoning framework that decides how much to accelerate each part of a demonstration. A pretrained language model uses the task instruction, visual context, and original motion of successive windows to select a speedup profile for the full episode. Experiments on LIBERO and RoboCasa-Kitchen show RePace outperforms baselines in overall task execution efficiency.

entry.title: Focusing on what matters: training-free focus maps for frozen vision transformers in long-video object segmentation
entry.summary: Focus Only on What's Important: Training-Free Focus Maps for Frozen Vision Transformers in Long-Video Object Segmentation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper addresses the high compute cost of vision transformers in video object segmentation by proposing a training-free focus map. Tracked object regions are processed at full resolution while other areas receive coarser token merging, using a union of velocity-shifted and block-matched masks, a camera-compensated surprise check, and a fallback merger when objects are lost. On the LVOS V2 long-video benchmark, the method outperforms ALGM in accuracy with 16% fewer counted encoder FLOPs, sitting close to the dense-encoder baseline. The authors note that lower counted compute did not reduce measured Cutie step time in their latency tests.

entry.title: BOP-Refer: A Benchmark for Locating Objects in 3D and 2D from Single Images
entry.summary: BOP-Refer: Benchmark for Monocular 3D and 2D Object Grounding arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces BOP-Refer, the first benchmark for locating referred everyday and industrial objects in single images using both 3D and 2D bounding boxes, drawn from nine BOP datasets. Images are paired with referring expressions generated by vision-language models and verified by humans, with ground-truth boxes derived from 3D models and 6DoF pose annotations. Evaluating 17 frontier models, the best one, Gemini 4 Carbon, scores 72.6% AP_IoU2D in 2D but only 12.4% AP_IoU3D in 3D.

entry.title: DocDUR-Net: A unified network that restores document images by sensing their degradations
entry.summary: DocDUR-Net: Degradation-Aware Unified Document Image Restoration arXiv · Nov 26, 2026Photos of documents often suffer varied damage from uncontrolled imaging conditions, which makes text hard to read. DocDUR-Net is a unified restoration network that derives restoration guidance directly from the input image, so it can adapt without external task selection, and it also offers a manual mode with explicit task choice. On document image restoration benchmarks, it reports the best average PSNR of 29.405 dB and SSIM of 0.960 among unified methods, while remaining competitive with single-degradation methods.

entry.title: Fine-tuning Transformers to Make Cost-Sensitive Financial Decisions
entry.summary: From Prediction to Decision: Decision-Focused Fine-Tuning of Autoregressive Tabular Transformers for Cost-Sensitive Financial Events arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how to fine-tune an autoregressive transformer trained on tabular event streams, used for predicting events such as fraud, to optimize decisions rather than probabilities alone. The model's restricted softmax over label tokens is trained to maximize expected utility under an institution-specified, amount-scaled cost matrix, with a closed-form objective and gradient. A KL anchor to the pretrained model and an auxiliary language-modeling term preserve calibration and the generative model. A GRPO-style sampled variant is also proposed as an extension to trajectory-level rewards.

entry.title: TIDE-Flow: A Spike Optical Flow Method Using Fine-Grained Temporal and Displacement Evidence
entry.summary: TIDE-Flow: Fine-Grained Temporal Evidence and Structured Displacement Matching for Spike Optical Flow arXiv · Nov 26, 2026Spike cameras capture fast motion through an integrate-and-fire mechanism, but their binary streams encode accumulated illumination, which makes motion estimation difficult. The paper proposes TIDE-Flow, a framework that jointly uses Temporal Integration Evidence and Displacement Evidence Encoding for spike-based optical flow estimation. These components are placed in a difference-correlation recurrent refinement framework. Controlled ablation experiments are reported to validate the contribution of the temporal and displacement modeling.

entry.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
entry.summary: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces DRBench Pro, a benchmark that treats structured knowledge coverage as its main evaluation target for deep research agents. It builds knowledge trees from Wikipedia and generates research queries and evidence-grounded rubrics from sampled subgraphs, with agents receiving only the query. The benchmark contains 144 cases across 24 domains and 44,102 rubrics, measuring breadth and depth of coverage. Evaluating 16 agents, the best reached 57.04% overall coverage.

entry.title: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Evaluating Real-to-Simulation Transfer
entry.summary: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents Real2SimLab, a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer, which builds simulations from real-world observations. It evaluates a method by running its generated program and scoring the resulting simulation with each benchmark's original scorer, avoiding separate integrations per method and benchmark. The platform also provides a pipeline for creating training data and reward annotations, filtering out video recordings that appear in benchmarks to avoid contamination. It currently supports 47 coding agents and 5 non-agent methods across 6 benchmarks.

entry.title: Restoring the World to Time Series: Why Timestamps Matter in Reasoning
entry.summary: Put the World Back: Timestamps Matter in Time Series Reasoning arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper argues that current evaluations of LLM time series reasoning give events in chronological order and pre-matched to the series, so it is unclear whether models truly use timestamps. The authors treat timestamps as explicit indices linking numerical observations and external events to shared world states, and build a diagnostic protocol to separate timestamp-grounded reasoning from correlational shortcuts. Controlled interventions on 310 questions from two tasks show that accuracy can persist when timestamps are replaced or removed, while breaking event-series alignment causes systematic failures.

entry.title: Study on whether text-to-image models leave identifiable visual traces
entry.summary: Probing Visual Idiosyncrasies in Text-to-Image Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper examines whether images from leading text-to-image models can be traced to their source model and which visual features make this possible. A standard ResNet-50 identified the source among four open-source models, HiDream-O1-Dev, FLUX.2-dev, HunyuanImage-3.0, and Qwen-Image-2512, with 100.00% accuracy on held-out prompts, while human participants reached only 62.61% on the pairwise task. The distinguishing cues appear in low-level texture statistics, object layout, depth, albedo, and style preferences in image captions.

entry.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Learning Knowledge Base Structure from Questions
entry.summary: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how to build knowledge bases for large language model applications, where the knowledge base structure determines how information is retrieved and connected to answer questions. The authors propose Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent, which compares expected answers with responses from the current knowledge base, proposes structural edits each round, rebuilds the knowledge base, and keeps an edit only when the loss decreases. In experiments on large documents made of research papers, updated structures achieved higher mean Answer F1 on generated questions, with graph schemas also improving on human questions while knowledge cards declined.

entry.title: TrailMix: a training-free way to steer image generation toward the prompt
entry.summary: Diffusion Steering via Adaptive Reward Estimation and Resampling arXiv · Nov 26, 2026Text-to-image diffusion models sometimes omit objects, attributes, or relationships requested in a prompt. This paper proposes TrailMix, a training-free method that generates cheap preview images along parallel denoising trajectories, scores them against the prompt with an external judge, and resamples toward better outcomes. It outperforms existing baselines on three text-to-image benchmarks, with notable gains on rare multi-object compositions. The authors also extend it to targeted image editing and introduce SEAM-Bench to test whether semantic edits preserve other image content.

entry.title: Proverbs as a Window on Collective Prescriptions: A Computational Analysis of Nearly 50,000 English Proverbs
entry.summary: Proverbs As A Window On Collective Prescriptions arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces a computational framework that uses large language models, validated against human judgments, to analyze nearly 50,000 English proverbs. It maps their topics, assesses how prescriptive they are, and quantifies their advice on key dimensions of human judgment and behavior. Most proverbs give guidance on matters within individual control, while those about uncontrollable circumstances tend to describe rather than prescribe. On genuine trade-offs such as autonomy versus compliance, proverbs often give contradicting advice.

entry.title: Methods for repairing lost trustworthiness in compressed language models
entry.summary: Repairing the Trustworthiness of Distilled Language Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how compressing large language models into smaller distilled students can reduce trustworthiness even when downstream performance holds. It proposes a targeted repair framework based on the proximal Bregman response function, which estimates curvature with a surrogate proxy dataset instead of the original corpus. The framework is extended to preference-based supervision via an odds-ratio objective. Reported results show trustworthiness regressions improved by up to 8% with less than 1% increase in perplexity.

entry.title: Not all world models can doubt: how training objectives and architectures shape uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM
entry.summary: Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper compares epistemic uncertainty in two world model types: LeWorldModel, a JEPA that predicts embeddings without a decoder, and DreamerV3, an RSSM that reconstructs observations. Across ten simulated visual-control environments, the authors trace controlled state perturbations through each model to the final uncertainty estimate. They find that the RSSM's recurrent averaging and reconstruction objective attenuate the perturbation, so its uncertainty misses deviations its posterior registers, while the JEPA's uncertainty reflects what its model sees.

entry.title: Beyond Feature Fusion: Sensor-Grounded Semantic-Spiking Learning for Robust Object Detection
entry.summary: Beyond Feature Fusion: Sensor-Grounded Semantic-Spiking Learning for Robust Object Detection arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents SPIRE, a framework that detects objects robustly under varying illumination using a single spike camera stream. It builds appearance and cumulative views from the spike packet, with ANN features and spike-derived initialization setting membrane potentials and firing thresholds. On simulated VOC and COCO, SPIRE-D beats the strongest baseline by 4.00-5.50 AP50 points across four under- and overexposure settings. On real PKU-Vidar-DVS recordings it reaches 67.07 AP50 and 40.10 AP75, using 50.4% fewer MACs than SPFD.

entry.title: Gradient TD(λ) Extended to Non-Linear Function Approximation
entry.summary: Gradient TD(λ) for Non-Linear Function Approximation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026Temporal difference learning is central to reinforcement learning, but semi-gradient TD methods may diverge. Gradient TD algorithms use projection of the value function to provide convergent off-policy learning, though the λ-return version was limited to linear approximation. This paper extends that approach to non-linear function approximators, continuing to use the projected Bellman error as the objective.

entry.title: Routeability Audit Before LLM Routing Comparisons
entry.summary: Routeability Before Routing: Routeability Audit Protocol (RAP) and RouteabilityBench for Audited LLM Model Selection arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes RAP, a runnable audit protocol, and RouteabilityBench, a claim-verification package, to check whether a benchmark and model portfolio contain enough prompt-specific variation before routing methods are compared. Across four benchmarks and 66 LLMs, generic routing enhancements such as larger embedding sets, dimensionality reduction, selective abstention, clustering, and stronger regressors do not consistently beat the single best model. The authors recommend reporting routing gains alongside routeability diagnostics, tied-best analysis, portfolio details, and family-corrected statistical tests.

entry.title: LoopTitan: What Parameter Reuse Gives a Mixture-of-Experts Model
entry.summary: LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts? arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper examines looped Mixture-of-Experts models, which reuse layer parameters across depths to deepen the network without adding parameters. Using matched non-revisit controls, the authors find that parameter reuse itself contributes almost nothing; most gains come from network shape and residual scale. They propose LoopTitan-Base as a stronger standard MoE baseline and open-source LoopTitan with 17 pretrained models.

entry.title: VulnSafe: Measuring Vulnerability-Aware Relational Safety in Large Language Models
entry.summary: VulnSafe: Measuring Vulnerability-Aware Relational Safety in Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces VulnSafe, a Chinese capability assessment built around Vulnerability-Aware Response Competence (VARC), which breaks relational safety into five areas: risk perception, safety preservation, autonomy protection, supportive response, and boundary management. The assessment uses 41 scenarios with 2,050 balanced prompts and scenario-specific scoring rubrics, and separates proactive should-do behaviors from prohibitive should-not behaviors. Tests on eight representative LLMs show distinct competence profiles, with larger differences in proactive requirements than in prohibitive ones.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning for drone teams collecting sensor data when team size varies or drones fail
entry.summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi-UAV Data Harvesting Under Variable Team Sizes and Agent Loss arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes F-MADDPG, a flexible multi-agent reinforcement learning method that lets teams of UAVs harvest data from wireless sensors when the numbers of sensors and UAVs vary. It also handles catastrophic failures that permanently remove agents during a mission. Compared with a MADDPG baseline using multilayer perceptrons, F-MADDPG learns across the evaluated population sizes and completes missions faster on average. The authors report that inverse-cardinality team-size sampling outperforms uniform sampling and that the method remains effective after permanent agent losses.

entry.title: Transferring a network's optimization prior from another architecture
entry.summary: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper treats a network's initial geometry as an optimization prior and asks whether a target network can adopt a different architecture's prior. Before training, the target network is aligned to the representational geometry of a randomly initialized guide network, without transferring features, using gradients, or using labels. Aligning shallow networks to deeper ones and coarse-representation networks to fine-resolution ones improved downstream performance of the target network in both cases.

entry.title: Solving Vision with Code: Coding Agents Versus Video Models for Visual Reasoning
entry.summary: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper compares video generation models with coding agents on visual reasoning tasks. Given a first frame and a prompt, video models generate the answer video directly, while agents write programs that render it, with both scored by the same rule-based evaluator. On the 500-instance VBVR-Pro-Bench, three closed-model agents scored about 0.89 to 0.92, each well above the strongest video model. The authors conclude that for tasks whose solutions can be computed from a first frame and prompt, program synthesis is currently a more reliable route to visual reasoning than video generation.

entry.title: HOG-WAM: Making Robot Policies More Robust to Visual Noise by Predicting Future Gradients
entry.summary: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces HOG-WAM, a world-action model that adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients as structural supervision derived from demonstration images. An auxiliary HOG diffusion transformer is used only during training and removed at inference. Evaluated on RoboTwin-Plus and LIBERO Plus with visual corruptions, HOG-WAM achieves higher success than compared policies under the tested corruptions, with comparable performance on clean scenes.

entry.title: WorldExpand: Building Consistent 3D Worlds from Sparse Panoramic Views
entry.summary: WorldExpand: Building Coherent 3D Worlds via Sparse Joint Panoramic Expansion arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents WorldExpand, a method for building complete 3D scenes from a single panorama. Instead of densely generating sequential panoramic video frames, it generates a few complementary, high-resolution panoramas at informative locations, using coverage-guided view selection and joint panoramic diffusion based on Gaussian-splatting geometric warps. Experiments show it recovers content behind occluders and distant corners, improves novel-view synthesis and 3D reconstruction metrics, and runs faster than the existing panoramic-video method.

entry.title: Smoothness of Deep Network Layers Measured by Barron Norms
entry.summary: Barron Smoothness for Layers in Deep Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper splits the approximation error analysis of deep neural networks into two steps: choosing optimal infinite-width limits for each layer, then optimally discretizing all layers into a finite-sized network. The authors show that, in expectation, the discretization problem is equivalently characterized by a layer-wise generalization of Barron norms. They also analyze the optimization landscape and show that local minima satisfy an equidistribution principle, similar to ideas used in adaptive spline and finite element approximation.

entry.title: Split-RL: Resolving Local Conflicts in Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Split-RL: Local Conflict Resolution in Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces Split-RL, a gradient boosting trees method for reinforcement learning that uses guidance labels to separate conflicting feedback across different regions of the state space. It aims to prevent contradictory gradient signals from interfering with each other, which standard neural networks cannot do. The authors test it on constrained and offline RL with mixed datasets, reporting that it meets episodic cost budgets while keeping competitive rewards and approaches expert performance offline.

entry.title: PersonaFactory: Styling User Prompts with a Synthetic Persona Bank
entry.summary: PersonaFactory: Stylistic User Prompt Augmentation with Synthetic Persona Bank arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents PersonaFactory, a pipeline that generates detailed user personas and uses them to rewrite existing user prompts in each persona's style, so synthetic training dialogues better resemble real user-AI communication. The authors release over 740,000 structured personas and about 1.24 million persona-styled conversations across 85 languages. They report that attribute-based style representations preserve intent better than free-text persona descriptions at comparable style fidelity, and that the resulting conversations perform comparably to original training data on capability benchmarks.

entry.title: SceneDesigner3D: Agent-Driven Evolutionary Search for Rearranging 3D Indoor Scenes
entry.summary: SceneDesigner3D: Agentic Evolutionary Search for Principled Rearrangement of 3D Indoor Scenes arXiv · Nov 26, 2026SceneDesigner3D is a method for rearranging 3D indoor scenes that produces diverse layouts following common interior design principles. It represents each rearrangement as an editable program and evolves candidate layouts using a vision-language model agent, checking their physical validity. Proposals are scored for prompt adherence and design principles such as balance, zoning, circulation, and clutter. On the SAGE-10k and SceneSmith datasets, it improves prompt adherence and computed design principle scores over baselines by up to 5.1% and 15.2%.

entry.title: Comparing deep learning models for classifying brain tumours in MRI scans
entry.summary: Comparative Study of Deep Learning Architectures for Brain Tumour Classification arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This study compares six deep learning models that classify brain MRI scans as healthy, meningioma, glioma, or pituitary tumour. It uses four public datasets and removes exact and near-duplicate images to avoid data leakage between training and testing. Under leakage-aware cross-validation, ShuffleNetV2 and EfficientNet-B0 perform best and are statistically indistinguishable. On a fully held-out dataset, accuracy drops for every model, with EfficientNet-B0 generalising best. The authors argue that in-distribution accuracy overstates real-world performance.

entry.title: Adaptive Reliability Reserves for Residential Battery Fleets: A Simulation Study of Market Value Versus Household Backup
entry.summary: Adaptive Reliability Reserves for Residential Battery Fleets arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper uses a 2024 Houston (ERCOT) replay to compare a fixed 20 percent residential battery reserve with a county-risk-threshold reserve. The threshold approach raised five-hour backup coverage from 75.0 to 86.5 percent and added about USD 10.2 in modeled annualized margin per home. The authors release the HomeFleet-ERCOT benchmark, controllers, and checkpoints to allow reproducible comparison of these tradeoffs.

entry.title: When Every Rollout Fails: A paper on splicing learner-conditioned options into agent RL training
entry.summary: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper addresses long-horizon agent tasks where every sampled trajectory earns zero reward, leaving group-relative reinforcement learning without a usable policy gradient. It introduces SPLICE, which online selects a splice point in a failed current-policy trajectory, generates bounded options, estimates their values through repeated current-policy continuations, and fits the policy on return-weighted local targets. Across SWE-bench Verified and BrowseComp-Plus with two policy families, SPLICE outperforms GRPO and full-trajectory guidance baselines in all four settings, improving over GRPO by 2.8 to 9.8 percentage points.

entry.title: DFly2: Sharing the target model's sparsity to speed up long-context speculative decoding
entry.summary: DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target's Sparsity arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper presents DFly2, a block-parallel draft model for speculative decoding on long contexts. Each draft layer reads the KV cache of its paired target layer at the fixed set of positions chosen by that layer's indexer, so it needs no scoring pass or cache of its own. On DS-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash and Hy4~flash, it accepts more tokens per step than DFlash and DSpark trained on the same recipe, with larger gains on long-context and agentic benchmarks. At high concurrency on DS-V4.1-Flash, its throughput is 62% and 81% higher on two 64K sets at matched per-user decode speed.

entry.title: When to Trust a PFN: Detecting Harmful Shift in Tabular Foundation Models
entry.summary: When to Trust a PFN: Detecting Harmful Shift in Tabular Foundation Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper addresses the problem that tabular prior-fitted networks (PFNs) can fail silently when data distributions shift at deployment. It proposes CALD, a lightweight unsupervised monitor that raises an alarm based on an anchor loss obtained by finetuning the decoder to disagree with test-set predictions while staying accurate on an in-distribution anchor set. Experiments on 14 datasets with tabular and structured shifts, using TabPFN and TabICL, show CALD matches or outperforms baselines on harmful shifts and produces markedly fewer false alarms on benign shifts.

entry.title: InterConRank: Joint Node Ranking Across Interconnected Heterogeneous Networks
entry.summary: InterConRank: Joint Node Centrality in Interconnected Heterogeneous Networks arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces InterConRank, a centrality algorithm that computes a separate ranking of nodes for each layer of an interconnected network.
