Directed dependencies determine which layers supply scores to each receiving layer, and all layers are updated together so scores can move across layers and then along internal links. The authors prove convergence of this joint update and evaluate it on four scholarly networks. On all four, it gives the highest rank correlations with h-index and total citations for nodes in the collaboration layer.

entry.title: One Model, Many Modes: Evolving System Prompt Ensembles for Creative Generation
entry.summary: One Model, Many Modes: Evolving System Prompt Ensembles for Creative Generation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper argues that preference-aligned LLMs suffer from mode collapse, concentrating outputs on a narrow set of high-reward responses, which limits creative generation. It proposes SEPO, a training-free framework that evolves prompts and uses greedy max-min selection to pick behaviorally distinct system prompts under a quality constraint, then samples one prompt per response at inference. Across four creative tasks and three open-weight models, SEPO ranks first in 8 of 12 settings on the harmonic mean of quality, diversity, and novelty, with average quality decreasing while diversity and novelty rise.

entry.title: Detecting Backdoors by Comparing Fine-Tuned Models to Their Base Models
entry.summary: Reading Fine-Tuning Diffs Through Lenses: Model Diffing for Backdoor Detection arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes a common token-based scoring system to compare weight, activation, and output methods for detecting backdoors introduced during fine-tuning. It enhances existing weight and activation methods using the J-lens and its refinement, the J++-lens. In experiments comparing a backdoored model with its base model, the weight difference decoded through the J++-lens ranks the backdoor token in the top ten in 11 of 12 settings. The authors also show that each method can be evaded by a different attack, and no single method resists both.

entry.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Efficient Training Method for Long-Horizon Agents
entry.summary: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper addresses the high cost of on-policy distillation (OPD) for long-horizon agents, where each update requires fresh environment rollouts. It proposes CARE-OPD, which uses student-seeded teacher completions and response-level confidence gating to widen history coverage while filtering unreliable updates, and hindsight replay allocation that selects consequential turns using downstream execution evidence. On Software Engineering and Deep Research tasks, CARE-OPD outperforms online OPD and prior prefix replay baselines. On SWE-bench Verified, it reaches 59.5% task success while cutting end-to-end training time by 45% and environment actions by 44% relative to asynchronous online OPD.

entry.title: AutoRSP: An AI Agent That Automatically Designs Radar Sensing Pipelines
entry.summary: AutoRSP: An AI Agent for Radar Sensing Pipeline Design arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents AutoRSP, an AI agent that automatically designs radar sensing pipelines. It uses sub-agents mapped to five stack layers and represents each layer as code with modeled cross-layer dependencies. Its search is guided by feedback from realistic RF simulation, on-sensor emulation, and execution on edge devices rather than an LLM judge. Evaluated on robotic imaging, automotive perception, and vital sign sensing, it produces executable pipelines with performance comparable to or better than human-expert and closed-source agent pipelines.

entry.title: How Much Is a Theory Worth to an LLM Solver? Measuring, Inducing, and Merging Theories
entry.summary: What Is a Theory Worth to an LLM Solver? Measuring, Inducing, and Merging Theories in Context arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how much a stated mathematical theory helps a large language model solve problems, and whether models can write such theories themselves. In a length-matched test, adding the right theory raised Qwen3-14B's pass@1 on pattern waiting-time problems from 0.37 to 0.83 and reduced the median tokens of correct solutions, while same-length worked examples gave no benefit. The authors also plant unpublished theorems to measure how much of this gain induced theories recover, and find that merging several induced notes recovers more than any single note.

entry.title: SOLVE: Sparse ordered keyposes let LLM agents control robots versatilely and efficiently
entry.summary: SOLVE: Sparse, Ordered Keyposes Make LLM Agents Versatile and Efficient Robot Manipulator arXiv · Nov 26, 2026SOLVE is a training-free robot manipulation agent in which a multimodal LLM writes a sparse, ordered sequence of 6-DoF end-effector keyposes, observes the result, and writes the next, while a motion planner interpolates between them. It reports 74.5% success on RoboDojo and 84.5% on RoboLab at about $1.7 per episode, and 88% success over 16 zero-shot tasks on a real robot.

entry.title: BRIAR: Martingale-based belief smoothing over reasoning trees for guiding RL rollouts
entry.summary: BRIAR: Martingale Belief Smoothing on Bifurcation-Guided Reasoning Trees arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes BRIAR, a tree-structured framework for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards that targets long-chain reasoning. It expands reasoning trees along an outcome-bifurcation frontier and estimates latent node values via linear-time two-pass Rauch–Tung–Striebel smoothing. It also assigns suffix advantages only after an answer is absorbed, leaving earlier derivations unchanged.

entry.title: How well do vision-language scene graphs work as memory for embodied question answering?
entry.summary: How Well Do Vision-Language Scene Graphs Serve as Memory for Embodied Question Answering? arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper examines whether scene graphs can serve as memory for embodied question answering in a simulated multi-room setting. It defines answerability as the share of questions a fixed rule-based reader answers correctly from the graph alone. Four targeted repairs doubled recall and raised answerability from 27.2% to 37.4%, though higher object F1 did not always raise answerability. In one real-video test, graph memory lowered accuracy.

entry.title: Was the Model Given the Right Action? Auditing Action Input Handling in Navigation World Models
entry.summary: Was the Model Given the Right Action? Auditing and Repairing Action Interfaces in Navigation World Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper audits how actions are encoded for Navigation World Models (NWM) during evaluation compared with training, and finds three interacting mismatches. Correcting the inputs without retraining reduces mean visual prediction error by 42% on the RECON dataset, measured with DreamSim. The authors also introduce ActRosetta, a tool that checks whether action encoding matches training and repairs inputs when sufficient information is available.

entry.title: WorldInteract: Controllable video generation for interactions between different materials
entry.summary: WorldInteract: Controllable Streaming Video Generation for Multi-Material Interactions arXiv · Nov 26, 2026WorldInteract is a streaming video generation framework that models how different materials interact when pushed or in contact. It splits the task into generating material-dependent behavior and computing contact responses, linked through a shared velocity-increment interface. The generator is trained on 30k simulated videos without interactions across 22 material classes, and refined with Material-Aware RL using verifiable physical rewards. The paper reports substantial gains over state-of-the-art methods on Physics-IQ and more reliable push control on real-world images.

entry.title: Hierarchical Graph Metanetworks: metanetworks that process neural network weights by following their layered structure
entry.summary: Hierarchical Graph Metanetworks arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces Hierarchical Graph Metanetworks (H-GMNs), which process neural network weights by coarsening and refining a graph that follows the input model's layer, block, and module hierarchy. The method uses permutation-symmetry-preserving pooling and un-pooling layers and is extended to Transformers. Evaluated on ResNet-18 and ViT model zoos for tasks such as model evaluation, backdoor detection, and pruning, H-GMNs are reported to be more sample-efficient than non-equivariant and flat graph metanetworks, with cost staying nearly constant as depth grows.

entry.title: Bigger Model or Bigger Table? How Much Backbone a Chorus N-gram Module Replaces
entry.summary: Bigger Model or Bigger Table? How Much Backbone a Chorus N-gram Module Replaces arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper asks how much of a transformer's backbone the Chorus N-gram module can replace. Chorus adds hashed tables of token bigrams and trigrams to the model's input and attention. The authors trained models from 16M to 349M parameters on 1.34 billion tokens of Polish printed before 1918. With tables about as large as the backbone, Chorus matched plain models 1.16 to 1.34 times its size, with each added parameter replacing at most 0.31 backbone parameters.

entry.title: LiDAR intensity reconstruction with little real data: a fixed-epoch architecture benchmark
entry.summary: LiDAR Intensity Reconstruction with Limited Real Data: An Architecture Benchmark under Fixed-Epoch Training arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper benchmarks nine neural architectures that reconstruct LiDAR intensity from depth, semantic labels, incidence angle, and material reflectance, using real SemanticKITTI and synthetic VoxelScape data. All models were trained for a fixed 20 epochs. With real-only training, UNet-V2 achieved the best reconstruction metrics, followed by a denoising diffusion model (DDPM). In several mixtures with 1–10% real data, DDPM showed lower error and higher image-quality scores than the deterministic alternatives evaluated.

entry.title: Robust Recourse When Causal Graphs Are Ambiguous
entry.summary: Robust Recourse under Causal Graph Ambiguity arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies causal algorithmic recourse, which recommends actions to reverse unfavorable decisions, when several causal graphs fit the same data yet predict different effects for one action. The authors propose Worst-Case Recourse and Graph-Weighted Recourse to find low-cost actions that succeed across all candidate graphs or a specified fraction of graph weight. In benchmarks, relaxing robustness increases the number of valid recommendations and lowers costs, but reduces true successes, showing a coverage-validity trade-off.

entry.title: Calibrated Alzheimer's Diagnosis with Missing Test Data via Teacher-Guided Distillation
entry.summary: Privileged On-Policy Distillation for Calibrated Alzheimer's Diagnosis With Missing Modalities arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper addresses Alzheimer's diagnosis when some clinical, biospecimen, or imaging tests are missing. The proposed method, Graded Rollout Imputation with Privileged teachers, has the model fill in missing modalities one at a time, while teachers that use information available only during training grade the fills and supply a soft diagnostic target. The resulting model diagnoses from a single rollout and reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on the ADNI cohort, while remaining competitive and well calibrated on two external cohorts.

entry.title: Reads frozen vision model knowledge to detect AI-generated images without adapting the backbone
entry.summary: Reading, Not Adapting: Unlocking Frozen Visual Knowledge for AI-Generated Image Detection arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper proposes ReMoT, a framework that keeps a visual foundation model fully frozen and reads complementary detection evidence from spatially aligned RGB and wavelet views. It uses staged joint attention and learnable fusion queries to extract this evidence across Transformer depth without modifying the backbone. ReMoT uses 3,074 trainable parameters and reports 91.2% average accuracy across eight benchmark groups.

entry.title: Two-stage forecasting for new entities in temporal knowledge graphs
entry.summary: From Shared Patterns to Individual Evidence: Two-Stage Reasoning for Emerging Entities in Temporal Knowledge Graphs arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper addresses forecasting for emerging entities in temporal knowledge graphs, whose interaction histories start with no data and become sparse and bursty. It proposes INSPIRE, a two-stage framework: a shared-pattern predictor learned over the full candidate catalog, then a frozen predictor paired with a lightweight individual-evidence adapter. Across four benchmarks built on ICEWS and GDELT, INSPIRE improves Emerging MRR by 16.73% to 88.83% over the strongest baselines, and the adapter adds further gains over the Stage I predictors.

entry.title: When the Proxy Is Wrong: Bandits That Correct a Small Model's Data Choices
entry.summary: When the Proxy Is Wrong: Mismatch-Corrected Bandits for Adaptive Data Sampling arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how a small proxy model can choose training data for a larger target model when the proxy ranks data differently from the target. The authors model this mismatch as a multi-fidelity bandit, using frequent proxy rewards and rare paired target audits to correct the proxy. They provide regret bounds and a sliding-window policy that spreads audits over training. On CivilComments-WILDS, the method improves worst-group accuracy over a target-only policy at the same audit count.

entry.title: Maco-RL: Scaling Agent Abilities via Mixed-Task Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Maco-RL: Scaling Agent Capabilities with Mixed-Task Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes Maco-RL, a method for scaling mixed-task reinforcement learning (MixRL), which trains one unified policy across multiple domains without separate specialist models or a distillation stage. It uses a quota-based scheduler for asynchronous rollouts across task domains and Tri-Buffer Sampling (TBS) to allocate compute among samples of varying mastery. Experiments on five benchmarks show Qwen3.5-27B's overall score rising from 43.6 to 54.2, and to 60.1 with continual expansion, using less policy-update compute than single-task RL.

entry.title: How shifting class proportions changes classifier curvature
entry.summary: Effect of class proportion shifts on classifier curvature arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This study examines whether changing the share of two target classes in ten-class CIFAR-10 training alters the trace of the loss Hessian with respect to output-layer parameters. When the target class share rose from 10% to 19%, the trace fell by 0.152% on average, and when it fell to 1%, the trace rose by 0.071%. The authors also proposed a forecast based on initial class gradients, which in a prospective test gave a mean absolute error of 0.022 percentage points for direct increases, outperforming zero-change and equally weighted gradient forecasts.

entry.title: Context-aware remote sensing VQA via grounded on-policy distillation
entry.summary: Seeing the Right Context: Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Remote Sensing arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper addresses remote sensing visual question answering, where multimodal large language models must reason about targets using their surrounding objects and structures. The authors build GeoContext-5K, a dataset of 5,394 training pairs with explicit spatial cues, visual facts, and supporting regions. They propose GeOPD, an on-policy distillation method that uses these annotations, and report gains over open-source models and matched baselines on five benchmarks, improving the 4B and 9B base models by 5.81 and 2.97 points on average.

entry.title: A Failure-Driven Data Flywheel for Post-Training Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary: A Failure-Driven Data Flywheel for Post-Training Vision-Language-Action Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper proposes a failure-driven data flywheel for post-training pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models. It inserts task-relevant entities into reconstructed real-world scenes to create missing target scenarios, evaluates the model against each behavioral requirement, and allocates more data generation to conditions where failures persist. The framework is applied to autonomous driving scenarios involving occluded-pedestrian emergence and yielding at stop-sign intersections, tested in simulation and on a real vehicle.

entry.title: PoVi: Agentic Framework for Turning Poems into Knowledge-Grounded Videos
entry.summary: PoVi: Agentic Poetry-to-Video Generation with Knowledge Grounding and Figurative Understanding arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces PoVi, a benchmark and agentic framework for generating videos from poems. It rebuilds the poem's meaning into an evidence-bounded representation, then converts it step by step into narration, interpretation, character assets, and shot-level visual plans before generating narration-aligned video. Tested with three planning backbones and four video generators, PoVi outperforms single-call generation, with the largest gains on implicit background knowledge and metaphorical relations.

entry.title: Predicting evacuation traffic across multiple hurricanes with a generalizable graph learning model
entry.summary: Evacuation Traffic Prediction for Dynamic Transportation Networks over Multiple Hurricanes: A Generalized Graph Learning Approach arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents a generalized dynamic graph learning framework that uses traffic detector and evacuation data from 12 historical hurricanes. A GCN-LSTM model predicts evacuation traffic up to 6 hours ahead. For the unseen 2024 Hurricane Milton, it achieves an RMSE of 280.6 and R2 of 0.96 for 1-hour prediction, and RMSE of 459.8 and R2 of 0.89 for 6-hour prediction. The dynamic model reduces RMSE by 8.4% compared with its static counterpart and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

entry.title: MEG2text: Non-invasive brain-to-text decoding beyond alignment
entry.summary: Technical Report MEG2text: Beyond Alignment in Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This technical report presents MEG2text, a system that decodes language from non-invasive brain activity without surgery. It combines corrected training and evaluation, brain-text alignment, a class-balanced word readout, and target-word language-model fusion. On the LibriBrain100 word-ranking task it reaches 64.12% mean Top-10 balanced accuracy, 16.92 percentage points above the published MEG-XL across four corpora. Controlled comparisons indicate that both the implementation corrections and the learned readout contribute to the gain.

entry.title: Finding Visual Clues for Recognizing Entities in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper analyzes how well thinking vision-language models recognize entities in images when answering knowledge-based visual questions. It finds that most errors come from misrecognizing the entity, and that recognition depends on distinctive visual clues that help recall the entity. The authors propose ClueRL, a reinforcement learning method that focuses the advantage signal on these entity-recall clues in the reasoning trace. The method outperforms GRPO and a perception-reward baseline on three entity recognition benchmarks, and its gains extend to knowledge-based question answering and general multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: Neural Rendering Compiler: Using Video Generators as Programmable Renderers
entry.summary: Neural Rendering Compiler: Generative Video Models as Programmable Renderers arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper presents the Neural Rendering Compiler (NeurCo), which automatically probes frozen video generation models to build a manual of the semantic requirements each model can reliably satisfy. User intent is first expressed in a model-agnostic representation of objects, constraints, events, and cameras, then compiled into model-specific strategies: reliable requirements are kept, while unreliable ones are rewritten or handled differently. The authors also introduce VComBench, a benchmark of 380 multi-requirement tasks, and report improved requirement satisfaction on Wan and Minimax H3.

entry.title: Provably efficient reinforcement learning for concave utilities using linear function approximation
entry.summary: Provably Efficient Concave Utility Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies concave utility reinforcement learning (CURL), a framework that generalizes standard RL, imitation learning, and maximum entropy exploration. It works in finite-horizon episodic bilinear MDPs, estimating occupancy measures through low-dimensional feature expectations within a model-based optimistic policy optimization framework called OCUPO. The on-policy version has a sample complexity of Õ(ε⁻⁴), while an off-policy version using a backward feature regression subroutine achieves Õ(ε⁻²), and the approach is also extended to linear MDPs.

entry.title: DemoFoundry: Automatically Generating Realistic Robot Training Demonstrations
entry.summary: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering arXiv · Nov 26, 2026DemoFoundry is an automated framework that uses coding agents and generative rendering to create photorealistic, physically grounded robot demonstrations. Agents build paired real and proxy videos to train a video renderer, and write control programs that run in a physics simulator to produce proxy videos with aligned robot states and actions. A renderer then converts these proxies into scene-consistent realistic observations, and automated checks keep only successful trajectories. Experiments report better visual quality and action-video consistency, and policies trained on the generated demonstrations outperform raw-simulation training and approach the performance of training on an equal number of real demonstrations.

entry.title: Preparing Language Models for Compression at Any Budget Without Retraining
entry.summary: Learning to Be Truncated: Preparing LLM Checkpoints for SVD Compression arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces LLift, a method that prepares a pretrained model for SVD compression across different compression ratios without per-ratio fine-tuning. It fine-tunes a low-rank approximation at one ratio using the original model as a teacher, then merges the learned updates back into the original weights. On LLaMA-7B, a single prepared model shows accuracy gains at three compression ratios.

entry.title: Counting Video Repetitions Using Codec Motion with Frozen Diffusion VLMs
entry.summary: Counting Beyond Frames: Codec Motion Tells Frozen Diffusion VLMs How Many arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper addresses counting repeated events in videos, a task where models that sample only a few frames struggle because repetitions occur between frames. It uses block displacement motion already recorded by video codecs, treating each candidate count as a testable motion hypothesis. The proposed training-free framework, CoDiCount, reweights a frozen diffusion vision-language model's answer probabilities during denoising. The authors report consistent gains over official decoders on MotionBench, TOMATO, and SVCBench.

entry.title: Can LLM Coding Agents Replace RL by Reading World Models?
entry.summary: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model? arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper examines an alternative to reinforcement learning in which LLM-based coding agents read environment source code as a readable world model and directly synthesize control policies. The agents iteratively refine these policies using online feedback or offline data, without task-specific RL training. Experiments on diverse decision-making benchmarks show the synthesized policies match or outperform conventional RL methods while requiring substantially less experience.

entry.title: Atunda: An AI-ready video dataset of Afrogenic dance moves for automatic movement classification
entry.summary: Atunda: Building an Afrogenic Dance Movement Dataset for AI-Driven Classification arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents Atunda, the first systematically collected video dataset of Afrogenic dance moves, built for training and evaluating deep learning models that classify movement. Its first phase includes nearly 400 videos covering 13 dance moves from African and African Diaspora performance culture. Using temporal convolutional neural networks, the authors report classification accuracy above 95%, providing a baseline benchmark for future research.

entry.title: REE: A Benchmark Testing AI Agents on Scientific Research
entry.summary: REE: A Scientific Research Entrance Exam for AI Agents arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces REE (Research Entrance Exam), a benchmark of 100 open-ended research problems spanning five scientific areas and 23 domains, each drawn from active research and reviewed by domain experts. Agents have up to 12 hours to iteratively improve a working starter solution, which is scored against an expert solution under comparable conditions. The authors report that Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol outperform the expert solutions on 86% and 81% of problems respectively.

entry.title: Hard background pairings that transfer across classifiers and images
entry.summary: A Hard Background Pairing Transfers across Classifiers and Images arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper tests image classifiers on composite images that paste objects onto backgrounds from other photographs. The authors split 40 ImageNet classifiers into two halves, used one half to pick the hardest pairing of object and background labels from COCO, and checked it on the other half. On composites from new photographs, mean accuracy fell from 50.3% on random pairings to 43.7% on the hardest pairing.

entry.title: Motion Beyond Pixels: Future Visual Features for Object Movement Prediction
entry.summary: Motion Beyond Pixels: Learning Future Visual Representations for Object-Centric Dynamics arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents MotionRep, a world model that jointly predicts future DINO visual features and 3D object flow, linking semantic and geometric information to object-centric dynamics. It also introduces DINO-VAE, which compresses DINO features in time and channels with latent regularization to produce compact latents. On simulated and real-world manipulation benchmarks, MotionRep outperforms pixel-based baselines in 3D object flow accuracy and generalization to unseen scenes, needing only three denoising steps at inference.

entry.title: Distractor-robust RL via variational bisimulation: replacing pixel reconstruction with an adversarial objective so latent states keep only task-relevant information
entry.summary: Distractor-Robust Reinforcement Learning via Variational Bisimulation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces VIBES, an objective that replaces pixel reconstruction with an adversarial term requiring latent states to predict both rewards and the next latent state. The authors argue this objective measures how far an encoder is from reward and dynamics sufficiency, and that its global optima induce bisimulation relations on histories when exact sufficiency is attainable. The method serves as a drop-in replacement for Dreamer's model-learning component, achieving state-of-the-art results on the Distracting Control Suite and extending to visually complex manipulation in Realistic ManiSkill.

entry.title: PRAM: Using Part-by-Part Reasoning to Unlock Hidden Multimodal Knowledge
entry.summary: PRAM: Activating Latent Multimodal Knowledge through Partwise Reasoning arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes PRAM, a method that transfers knowledge between data types, such as images and text, without paired training examples. It works on frozen encoders by combining statistical relationships between local parts through a shared pivot modality, and uses three modules for covariance regularization, spectral relational reasoning, and score fusion. According to the paper, PRAM achieves state-of-the-art results in 16 classification settings and 19 retrieval settings across ten datasets, and is highly competitive in three sensing scenarios.

entry.title: Checking whether removing a vision-model feature has the same effect across autoencoder training seeds
entry.summary: Carrying Feature Ablations Across Sparse Autoencoder Seeds arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies features learned by sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on layers of vision encoders such as DINOv2 and SigLIP. The authors remove a feature and its matched counterpart from an SAE trained with a different random seed, then compare how each removal changes the encoder's output on held-out images. The removal carries across seeds for 12% to 70% of matched pairs in three settings, and 0% in control settings. Predicting which removals carry is more accurate using layer contributions than feature directions, though some errors remain and output measurement catches what this screening misses.

entry.title: ZeroHero: Training Small Language Agents From Scratch
entry.summary: ZeroHero: Training Small Language Agents from Scratch arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces ZeroHero, a framework for training small language agents with fewer than 50 million parameters from scratch. A large language model serves as the expert, whose successful trajectories are used to pretrain the agent, which is then post-trained with proximal policy optimization and expert supervision on its generated language. The agents were tested in Crafter, WebShop, and Alfworld-Dialogue, approaching expert performance on WebShop and surpassing their demonstration experts on Crafter training rollouts and held-out Alfworld-Dialogue tasks.

entry.title: Using causal machine learning to predict acute food crises and identify actionable drivers
entry.summary: Predicting acute food crises and discovering actionable drivers with causal machine learning arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper enriches the open Harmonized Food Insecurity Dataset with driver variables covering 80 countries monthly at subnational level from 2007 to 2024. It builds machine learning pipelines resilient to missing data to forecast crisis occurrence 3, 6, and 9 months ahead, using FEWS NET and IPC/CH classifications. The pipelines outperform no-skill baselines by 15 to 50 percentage points in PR-AUC. Comparing predictive importance with causal estimates, the authors find that conflict events, with the weakest predictive signals, are primary causal drivers, while agroclimatology is the only dimension where both align.

entry.title: DecisionReplay: A Dataset and Offline Simulator for Testing Ensembles of Decision Models
entry.summary: DecisionReplay: A Corpus and Offline Simulator for Ensembling Decision Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces DecisionReplay, a dataset of answer-option probability vectors from 17 commercial decision models across 35 benchmarks, with token counts, billed cost, and latency for every call. A deterministic simulator replays ensemble, router, and cascade policies without new model calls. The authors report that one well-chosen model per benchmark is hard to beat, and that certified early exit reduces stacked-ensemble cost without changing answers.

entry.title: HoMe: Practical Optimization of Memory Harnesses for AI Assistants
entry.summary: HoMe: Toward Practical Harness Optimization of Memory Systems for AI Assistants arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents HoMe, an evaluation-driven framework that iteratively improves the harness of a memory system for long-running AI assistants. The harness includes the code, prompts, and configurations used for memory construction, maintenance, retrieval, and answer generation. HoMe uses session-level memory versioning and execution traces to find shared failures and reduces evaluation cost through smoke tests, adaptive sampling, and memory reuse. Validated on the open-source ReMe system with LongMemEval-S and BEAM benchmarks, it finds harnesses that outperform the original on end-task performance while using far fewer query-time tokens.

entry.title: Beyond Pose Control: Consistent Anatomy in Ultrasound Video Generation
entry.summary: Beyond Pose Control: Anatomically Consistent Ultrasound Video Generation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies generating ultrasound videos conditioned on probe pose, which is hard because tracked scans are scarce. The authors argue that pose control alone yields implausible anatomy in unscanned regions and inconsistent anatomy on revisits. They combine an anatomical prior built from many subjects, refined online during generation, with a 3D latent memory that accumulates slices into a patient volume. Experiments on thyroid, kidney, and lumbar spine report gains in visual fidelity, pose following, and anatomical consistency.

entry.title: Automatically choosing batch variables to harmonize radiomic features
entry.summary: Automated Batch-Variable Selection for ComBat-Based Radiomic Harmonization arXiv · Nov 26, 2026ComBat can correct batch effects in multicentre radiomic features, but batch variables are usually chosen by hand without a standard rule. This paper proposes ParsiComBat, which ranks acquisition parameters by batch effect, removes redundant ones, and scores sequential ComBat corrections. It balances removing technical variation against preserving feature structure and makes no correction when technical variation is negligible. In simulations, CT and MRI cohorts, and clinical prediction tests, it reduced batch effects without significantly changing clinical discrimination.

entry.title: Learning Conditional Independence Graphs from Dependent Time Series via Time-Delay Embedding
entry.summary: Conditional Independence Graph Learning from Dependent Data Via Time-Delay Embedding arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how to infer the conditional independence graph of high-dimensional stationary multivariate Gaussian time series that may be short-range or long-range dependent. It uses time-delay embedding, treating each series and its delayed copies as a multi-attribute random vector at each node. A penalized pseudo log-likelihood with lasso or non-convex penalties is optimized by ADMM, with sufficient conditions for consistency and graph recovery established. Synthetic and real-data examples illustrate the approach.

entry.title: Commit2Drive: Making Language Driving Decisions Binding on the Planned Trajectory in Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary: Commit2Drive: Perception-Grounded Language Decisions as Commitments for Trajectory Planning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents Commit2Drive, a framework for Vision-Language-Action driving models that treats the language decision as a commitment constraining trajectory planning. The decision is a maneuver class with a continuous parameter, grounded in the model's own perception and mapped to a kinematic code. Consistency losses train the planner to follow the decision, and an automatic pipeline generates the supervision. On Bench2Drive, it reports a Driving Score of 78.50 and a Success Rate of 55.91% with a 0.5B language model, and greatly reduces language-action inconsistency.

entry.title: Is an LLM needed for weight-space programming? A deterministic forward-only method and its limits
entry.summary: Do We Really Need an LLM for Weight-Space Programming? A Deterministic Forward-Only Paradigm and Its Capability Boundaries arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper questions whether large language models are required for editing neural network weights using forward passes only. It proposes Forward Weight-Space Programming (FWSP), a deterministic pipeline with probing, localization, structured operators, automatic routing, and verification. The authors also introduce Protected FisherGate for reasoning models and report results across multiple models and modalities, along with proofs of two operator boundaries.

entry.title: DuCo: A Training-Free Sparse Attention Method Using Cross-Layer Consistency
entry.summary: DuCo: Exploiting Dual Cross-Layer Consistency for Sparse Geometric Attention arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper addresses the quadratic cost of dense global attention in visual geometry foundation models, which limits inference on long image sequences. It proposes DuCo, a training-free sparse attention framework that reuses historical attention information and clusters value representations to exploit redundancy across layers. Experiments on three visual geometry foundation models and five benchmarks show favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.

entry.title: Estimating spatially varying blur in fluorescence microscopy without calibration
entry.summary: Blind spatially varying PSF estimation for fluorescence microscopy arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents DeepBlur, a neural network that estimates spatially varying two-dimensional point spread functions directly from single images of biological structures. It is trained entirely on physical simulations covering aberrations, illumination and noise, and needs no user-supplied optical parameters. Using a deformable mirror, the authors acquired 1,290 images and found the estimates agree closely with independent references and improve deconvolution of experimentally aberrated images.

entry.title: Crowdsourced Labeling Learned With Unsupervised IRT Models
entry.summary: Learning from Crowds with Unsupervised Item Response Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper treats crowdsourced labeling as an unsupervised item response theory problem, with annotators as test takers and tasks as items. The authors evaluate unsupervised logistic IRT models on six datasets with crowdsourced labels and known ground truths, checking how well they recover traits and infer labels. They also propose using IRT models to inform classifiers during training and compare them with existing crowd-learning methods.

entry.title: Looks at Frames Repeatedly: YoloMT, a Real-Time Streaming Video Model That Runs on a T4 GPU
entry.summary: You Only Look Multiple Times: YoloMT, a Real-Time Streaming Model on a T4 arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents YoloMT, a 449.8M-parameter model for real-time streaming video captioning on a single GPU. It was distilled from a 27B teacher model using SFT and GRPO, and it reportedly leads all models under 1B parameters on OVO-Bench, MVBench, StreamingBench and Video-MME. Each frame is encoded once and cached as 16 tokens, so the model can use past frames without extra vision passes.

entry.title: SEAM: A self-evolving framework that automatically tests hallucinations in multimodal AI models
entry.summary: SEAM: A Self-Evolving and Adaptive Probing Framework for Automatic MLLM Hallucination Evaluation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents SEAM, a framework that automatically evaluates hallucinations in multimodal large language models instead of relying on fixed test items. It uses a library of ten probing skills, three elicitation wrappers, and five question formats, with an inner loop that adaptively generates and refines test items and an outer loop that updates skills from past probing. In experiments on four target models and ten hallucination types, SEAM achieved an 89.2% relative improvement in mean valid hallucination discovery rate over representative static benchmarks across 12 matched comparisons.

entry.title: μMPC: Microsecond-scale nonlinear and world-model control from edge devices to GPUs using Koopman-linearized precompilation
entry.summary: μMPC: Microsecond-Scale Nonlinear and World Model Control from Edge to GPU via Koopman-Linearized Precompilation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents μMPC, a fast model predictive control framework that reduces online computation by using learned Koopman-linearized dynamics. It precomputes finite-horizon control-to-output maps to yield an action-only quadratic program with Hn_u decision variables, independent of the lifted dimension. The authors report solve times as low as 23 microseconds on a desktop CPU and 24 ms on a 168 MHz Crazyflie microcontroller, and collision-aware planning for 200 quadrotors on a GPU. They state speedups of up to 108× for constrained MPC and 1907× for visuomotor planning over competing methods.

entry.title: ADClaw: A Programmable Visual Agent for Industrial Defect Detection and Understanding
entry.summary: ADClaw: A Programmable Visual Agent for Industrial Anomaly Detection and Understanding arXiv · Nov 26, 2026ADClaw is an inspection agent that tests anomaly hypotheses by writing and running code, without task-specific fine-tuning. A Structured Normality Prior identifies applicable rules and retrieves normal visual references, and the agent combines masks, anomaly maps, and measurements in a persistent workbench to run follow-up checks. The paper reports competitive detection and localization results on 2D and 3D industrial anomaly detection benchmarks and on anomaly understanding in MMAD.

entry.title: ChemoMAE: Self-supervised spectral learning maps chemical variation in historic wood
entry.summary: ChemoMAE: Self-Supervised Spectral Representation Learning Reveals Chemical Heterogeneity in Historical Wood arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces ChemoMAE, a self-supervised Transformer that learns pixelwise representations from near-infrared hyperspectral images through masked denoising. The authors applied it to transverse sections of 49 wood specimens from historical Japanese buildings, clustering the representations into spatial maps without predefined chemical categories. They also defined Local Label Agreement (LLA) to measure label consistency among neighboring pixels and proposed mechanistic hypotheses for internal and surface degradation.

entry.title: Tune for Retention, Not Just Gain: SFT Forgets Far Less Than Expected
entry.summary: Tune for Retention, Not Just Gain: SFT Forgets Far Less than You Think arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies catastrophic forgetting, the loss of previously learned abilities when language models are fine-tuned on new tasks. The authors find that maximizing new-task performance can cause forgetting, but lower learning rates and batch sizes can achieve similar gains with little forgetting. When hyperparameters are chosen for both gain and retention, vanilla supervised fine-tuning (SFT) performs competitively with Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT), an on-policy method designed to reduce forgetting, challenging the view that on-policy training is necessary for retention.

entry.title: Learning recruiter decision procedures as memory for multi-session hiring assistants
entry.summary: Procedure Inference as Memory: Learning Recruiter Decision Procedures from OKF-Structured Episodes in Multi-Session Hiring Assistants arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes Open Knowledge Format (OKF)-indexed episodic memory to organize hiring assistant interactions and retrieve related events through their lineage. It also introduces Procedure Memory, which learns reusable decision procedures from these episodes via prompted reflection or reinforcement learning. OKF-indexed retrieval outperforms full-history context and conversation search in the evaluated settings while using 69% fewer context tokens than full history. On PersonaMem-v2, Procedure Memory with OKF retrieval reaches 50.2% accuracy versus 48.6% for full-history context.

entry.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
entry.summary: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper examines how to scale medical multimodal large language models, finding that existing medical models often trail general-purpose frontier models and that larger size mainly improves text rather than visual perception. The authors introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter model with 3B activated parameters, trained with stage-specific data curation and a curriculum of pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and adaptive reinforcement learning. It scores 58.26% average on 31 public multimodal benchmarks across 238 clinical tasks, outperforming two cited models and approaching a proprietary model on several tasks. Complex medical reasoning and multi-step clinical workflows remain challenging.

entry.title: Recognizing Turbulence and Fractional Topological Charge from Vortex Beam Speckle with Deep Learning
entry.summary: Investigating the efficacy of vortex beam speckle patterns for the recognition of atmospheric turbulence and fractional topological charge with a deep learning model arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper asks whether a convolutional neural network can estimate the fractional topological charge of a vortex beam directly from a single speckle image, and at what turbulence strength this fails. The authors simulate beams propagated over 1500 m through von Kármán phase screens and scattered by a fixed diffuser. Charge is read accurately without turbulence, but error rises as turbulence increases, and the turbulence category is correctly identified in 78% of images.

entry.title: Physics-guided generative models for oxy-combustion flame images
entry.summary: Physics-Guided Generative Modelling of Oxy-Combustion Flame Images: From Conditional LSGANs to Denoising Diffusion Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper develops two deep generative models that map 15 continuous operating parameters to a 512×64 heat-release flame image, serving as surrogates for costly oxy-combustion burner experiments. Both models are trained on 1,609 samples from the OXYTEC dual-swirl non-premixed oxy-combustion database. A conditional least-squares GAN generates images in about 20 ms, while a denoising diffusion model improves with longer training but takes roughly thirty seconds per image.

entry.title: Black-box attack on image classifiers using a diffusion model guided by adversarial conditions
entry.summary: Score-based Black-box Attack via Adversarial Condition Guided Diffusion Model arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper adapts score-based black-box attacks to reverse diffusion, using only the victim model's output probabilities to guide latent updates without its gradients. It introduces adaptive-target guidance, which uses the victim's runner-up class as an adversarial condition, and target-search guidance, which finds a small perturbation of the original condition embedding. Experiments on the ImageNet-Compatible dataset report better attack effectiveness and image quality than transfer-based baselines.

entry.title: Edge-AI condition monitoring for predictive maintenance in dairy processing using explainable AI
entry.summary: On Utilization of Edge-AI for condition monitoring towards predictive maintenance: A use case in dairy processing using explainable AI arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper develops an Edge-AI-based condition monitoring framework as a step toward predictive maintenance. It targets a rotary valve in a dairy processing pilot plant. Vibration data is collected by a low-power Industrial IoT sensor node and processed on an edge device.

entry.title: Compact vision-language navigation for continuous environments using on-policy training and route-bearing output
entry.summary: Compact Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environmentsvia On-Policy Training and Route-Bearing Output arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents a 2-billion-parameter monocular RGB navigation policy that follows language instructions in continuous environments. It adapts Qwen3-VL-2B with low-rank adapters and processes an eight-frame memory plus the current view in one forward pass. The policy predicts the route direction as a bearing in the agent's body frame, which a deterministic controller converts into motion, allowing on-policy relabeling of visited states that the authors report improves success.

entry.title: M²AdaptVLA: A robot control model with multimodal memory and predictive test-time adaptation
entry.summary: M²AdaptVLA: Multimodal Memory-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Model with Predictive Test-Time Adaptation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents M²AdaptVLA, a vision-language-action model that combines visual and force-torque (wrench) histories for robotic manipulation. It adapts to shifts in contact dynamics at deployment through predictive test-time adaptation. On eight tasks requiring both visual and wrench memory, it achieves a mean success rate of 82.71%, a 31.46% absolute gain over the strongest baseline.

entry.title: Information-theoretic analysis of hiding information in semantic communication
entry.summary: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Information Hiding in Semantic Communication arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper builds an information-theoretic framework for information hiding in semantic communication by extending the classical hiding model to a two-layer semantic and syntactic structure with four distortion constraints. The capacity is formulated as a Stackelberg game with a single-letter maximin expression, supported by achievability and converse results. The authors find that semantic hiding is not unconditionally superior to classical hiding, as confirmed by binary, ternary, and Gaussian examples.

entry.title: Recalling past video evidence to answer present streaming questions
entry.summary: Recalling the Past to Answer the Present: Context-Aware Multi-Evidence Reasoning for Streaming Video Question Answering arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper introduces StreamRecall, a benchmark of 4,983 questions over 462 videos for evaluating how models retrieve and combine scattered evidence from video history to answer streaming queries. It also proposes the Evidence Utilization Cascade, which diagnoses reasoning through evidence localization, grounding, chain completion, and answer derivation. The authors present EviStream, a training-free causal visual memory that keeps critical evidence under a fixed KV budget. Experiments show substantial gaps between current vision-language models and realistic streaming requirements.

entry.title: HAS: A hierarchical adaptive frame sampling method for video understanding
entry.summary: HAS: Hierarchical Adaptive Frame Sampling for Video Understanding arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper addresses the problem that multimodal large language models cannot process full-length videos and must work with a subset of frames. It proposes HAS, a two-stage method that first selects query-relevant, non-redundant backbone frames using a Determinantal Point Process, then adaptively allocates the remaining frame budget to local and global context based on the backbone's temporal distribution. Integrated into three leading MLLMs, HAS reportedly performs consistently better on the Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU benchmarks.

entry.title: EPPC-CARE: Staged Annotation of Communication in Patient-Provider Messages
entry.summary: EPPC-CARE: Staged Hierarchical Annotation of Communication Behaviors in Secure Patient-Provider Messages arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents EPPC-CARE, an automated framework for identifying communication behaviors in secure patient-provider portal messages, along with the supporting text for each classification. It uses 5,516 reference annotations from 867 messages, each a span, code, and subcode triplet. Across six open-weight large language models, EPPC-CARE outperformed EPPC-OASIS, improving Triplet F1 by 2.90 percentage points on average, with a best score of 64.4%.

entry.title: Kant-Q: A Q-learning method for Kantian equilibrium in symmetric Markov games
entry.summary: Kant-Q: A Q-Learning Algorithm for Kantian Equilibrium in Symmetric Markov Games arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes Kant-Q, a Q-learning algorithm in which each agent learns joint actions where all agents play the same action, corresponding to a Kantian equilibrium where each agent plays the action it wants everyone to adopt. The authors prove that every symmetric Markov game has a pure Kantian equilibrium and that the agents' Q-tables converge to the same limit. In experiments on the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma and the GovSim fishery game with up to 200 agents, Kant-Q learns the Kantian equilibrium and outperforms the baselines.

entry.title: AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base: An Open Mixture-of-Experts Language Base Model
entry.summary: AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper presents AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base, a mixture-of-experts language model trained from scratch at Yandex and released under the Apache 2.0 license, with 80 billion total parameters and about 3 billion active per token. It is pretrained on 17.5 trillion tokens, followed by two context-extension stages and a stage for reasoning and agentic interaction. The authors also introduce and release two Russian-language factual knowledge benchmarks, WikiWebFacts and HardMultiQA, on which the model outperforms larger comparison models.

entry.title: Automatically Identifying Resilience Stages with Machine Learning to Quantify System Resilience
entry.summary: Resilience Analysis Through Automated Stage Identification and Quantitative Assessment arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes a machine learning approach that automatically recognizes PARA (Plan/Prepare, Absorb, Recover, Adapt) resilience stages from system-performance time series, regardless of domain or threat. Four models are compared: Random Forest, SVM, LightGBM, and XGBoost, and their predictions are used to compute resilience metrics. Tested on two network systems and an airport transportation system, the best stage-classification F1-scores range from 74.3% to 99.4%, and the best MAPE for the resilience metrics R_t and RL ranges from 0.35% to 9.56%.

entry.title: Rank first, then encode: reading only a few percent of a whole-slide image
entry.summary: Rank Before You Encode: Reading a Few Percent of a Whole-Slide Image arXiv · Nov 26, 2026Classifying a whole-slide pathology image requires encoding thousands of high-resolution tiles, which is the main inference cost. This paper keeps an existing full-bag model frozen and runs it only on selected tiles, comparing this with random sampling at the same encoder cost. A 3.3K-parameter selector is fitted to the frozen model's attention without extra slide labels. At (K,b)=(1000,10), encoding costs about 6.6% of the full bag, and AUROC drops by no more than 0.005 in 33 of 36 aggregator-task pairs.

entry.title: PURA: Pruning video tokens by judging space and time redundancy together
entry.summary: PURA: Video Token Pruning via Unified Spatiotemporal Redundancy Assessment arXiv · Nov 26, 2026Video large language models are costly to run because they process long sequences of visual tokens. PURA is a training-free method that prunes these tokens by assessing spatial and temporal redundancy in a unified way. It combines representation error with token importance to set each token's removal cost, and uses Coordinated Pruning to remove compatible low-cost tokens in batches. Experiments on three video large language models and five video understanding benchmarks show a favorable balance between task performance and inference efficiency.

entry.title: Feasibility-aware deep reinforcement learning for placing O-CU and O-DU components in 6G O-RAN
entry.summary: Feasibility-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for O-CU and O-DU Mapping in 6G O-RAN arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper examines how to place virtual network function components of the O-RAN central and distributed units onto virtual machines in 6G open radio access networks. It frames the task as a sequential decision problem that prioritizes placing as many components as possible, then using fewer active machines and less wasted resource. The authors compare deep Q-network and double deep Q-network methods against six baselines, including heuristics and a MILP solver. Results show the learning methods achieve high placement fractions, but simpler heuristics match that quality with lower cost and decision time, so superiority over conventional methods is not established.

entry.title: Using a Vision-Language Model's Decoder as a Probe to Describe and Steer Its Visual Representations
entry.summary: Decoder-as-a-Probe: Verbalizing and Steering Visual Representations in LVLMs arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces Decoder-as-a-Probe (DaP), which treats the LLM decoder of a large vision-language model as a classifier and uses its first-order Taylor expansion as a linear probe. It outperforms classical probing and steering baselines, especially when training data is sparse. DaP can verbalize what the model perceives in an image and selectively change perceived attributes such as color, clothing, or action.

entry.title: SMOTE at 25: A Review of Its Variants, Evidence, and Reach (survey of the SMOTE oversampling method and its derivatives)
entry.summary: SMOTE 25 Years of Magic: What Has Been Done, What the Evidence Shows, and Whom It Reached arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper reviews SMOTE, an oversampling method published in 2002, and the many variants built on it. The authors audited 76 papers, screened 22,426 search records, and analyzed datasets, comparisons with SMOTE, and applications. They report that many variants change only some of SMOTE's decisions, and that independent studies find the gains shrink with strong learners and tuned thresholds, while resampling can damage calibration. The paper closes with a selection guide, a fifteen-item reporting checklist and a research agenda.

entry.title: Angle Interpolation in Low-Dose CT Reconstruction: Placement and Step-Size Scaling
entry.summary: Angular Interpolation in Sparse-View Low-Dose CT Reconstruction: Placement Effects and Data-Consistency Step-Size Scaling arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how angular interpolation applied before learning affects sparse-view low-dose CT reconstruction, distinguishing its use for sinogram initialisation from its use as an image residual base. On synthetic parallel-beam data, interpolation cut missing-view mean absolute error at 60 views by 99.7% compared with zero filling. In a data-consistency dual-domain network, sinogram initialisation outperformed an image-only U-Net by 0.96 dB at 60 views and 10% dose, while the interpolated image base performed worse. The authors also report that the dominant gain of the projection/backprojection pair scales approximately with NK, supporting this normalisation for step calibration.

entry.title: Checking Whether Operational Logs Reveal Patient or Time Identity
entry.summary: Auditing Identity and Timing Signals in Operational Logs arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper introduces two audits that measure how much information an operational log dataset carries about which unit a record came from and when it was recorded, before any event-prediction model is trained. The author applies them to seven public datasets across six domains. In ICU data, carrying the last measurement forward raises identity recognition, and on a sepsis forecasting task it inflates apparent model performance under patient overlap. Timing features alone also score well on held-out patients.

entry.title: FlyingStart: Learned Warm Starts for Faster Decoding in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
entry.summary: FlyingStart: Learned Cross-Token Warm Starts for Fixed-Point Decoding in Recurrent-Depth Language Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Recurrent-depth language models generate each token by repeatedly applying a shared block of layers until the hidden state converges. This paper shows that the starting point of this iteration is a second factor, separate from the stopping rule, and that a token's fixed point can be predicted from the state where the previous token stopped after a learned coordinate change. The authors introduce FlyingStart, a linear warm start fitted in closed form on the frozen model at a cost under 5% of one loop. On Huginn-0125, it matches the strongest training-free baseline's accuracy with 14% to 19% fewer decoding layers and raises batched throughput by 16% to 18% in two serving engines.

entry.title: Where Fairness Gaps Hide in a Multimodal Video Moderation Pipeline
entry.summary: Where Does the Asymmetry Enter? Staging a Fairness Audit Across a Fused Multimodal Moderation Pipeline arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper audits a published TikTok video moderation classifier that fuses video, speech, and on-screen text, using source language as the subgroup axis. It tests three stages: what the model may read, what its text branch encodes, and its final decisions. Significant language asymmetries appear at the input-reading stage and in the text branch, while the final decision stage is too small to detect them. The authors argue that audits reading only decisions can miss disparities arising upstream.

entry.title: ProManO: Upgrading Feed-Forward 3D Geometry to Metric Scale Beyond Sim(3)
entry.summary: ProManO: Beyond Sim(3) for Metric Upgrade of Feed-Forward Geometry with Visual-Inertial Anchors arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper addresses how to align dense feed-forward geometry predictions to sparse metric anchors from visual-inertial odometry (VIO) to recover real scale. The authors prove that transformations compatible with pre-calibrated camera intrinsics form a ten-dimensional manifold, which extends beyond Sim(3) with three extra degrees of freedom for the plane at infinity. They propose ProManO, a probabilistic manifold optimization method that weights each anchor by its along-ray uncertainty and inlier probability within one EM procedure. Experiments on EuRoC, CID-SIMS, Oxford Spires, and KITTI-360 report the highest mean F1 and better results than Sim(3) alignment on all four datasets.

entry.title: Backpropagation reframed as Dirac-bracket dynamics for dissipative training
entry.summary: Backpropagation as Dirac-bracket dynamics of dissipative training arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper treats gradient-based training of a parametric model as a damped particle moving in the potential set by the loss. Using Bateman-Galley doubling of degrees of freedom, it writes gradient flow, the heavy-ball method and Nesterov's accelerated gradient method as Hamiltonian systems. It shows that within this description, backpropagation corresponds to Dirac evolution, with layer activations as phase-space coordinates and layer equations as constraints. Numerical tests confirm these results to machine precision, and a network is trained by integrating the Dirac flow of its constraints without a backward pass.

entry.title: Fast interactive medical volume rendering using feed-forward adaptive Gaussian splatting
entry.summary: Feed-Forward Adaptive Gaussian Splatting for Interactive Medical Volume Rendering arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper presents RenderFM-Next, a feed-forward model that predicts Gaussians once per CT or MR volume, so new transfer functions need no network rerun and clipping planes cut the Gaussians directly. It starts with coarse 3 mm Gaussians and refines selected ones to 1.5 mm where refinement improves the image. On a benchmark of about 2,000 CT and MR scans, it outperforms RenderFM retrained on the same data by 2.8 dB on CT and 2.4 dB on MR, rendering a 1600x1600 view in 4-6 ms.

entry.title: TACC: Target-aware compression that speeds up novel view synthesis from many input images
entry.summary: TACC: Target-Aware Carrier Compression for Dense-Context Novel View Synthesis arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces TACC, a compression module for feed-forward latent novel view synthesis that generates new views of a scene without per-scene optimization. It organizes each source view into a progressive carrier hierarchy and adaptively retrieves tokens based on geometric relevance between source and target views, producing a compact, target-conditioned representation. On the RE10K dataset under dense input settings, TACC achieves 9.23× and 64× higher Effective FPS than Full Context on LagerNVS and LVSM, respectively, with Effective FPS excluding one-time source encoding and carrier construction.

entry.title: DiversePlace: Diversity-Seeking Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Macro Placement
entry.summary: DiversePlace: Diversity-Seeking Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Macro Placement arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents DiversePlace, a reinforcement learning method for macro placement, an early chip design step that fixes large block locations. It keeps a compact archive of layouts that have competitive HPWL (wirelength) but differ meaningfully from each other, so later stages can choose among them. The method uses curriculum proximal policy optimization with a quality-gated diversity reward and an expanding placement horizon. On eight ISPD2005 benchmark designs, it improves top-5, top-10, and top-20 archive diversity while achieving equal or lower HPWL.

entry.title: HardPatch: a method for attacking vision-language AI models using only their outputs
entry.summary: Attacking Hard-Label Large Vision-Language Models with Model-Sensitive Adversarial Patch Designs arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces HardPatch, a hard-label attack on large vision-language models (LVLMs) that needs only query access and no gradients. It splits an image into patches, masks each one to measure how sensitive the model is to it, and then optimizes the most vulnerable patches in descending order of sensitivity. The authors report that experiments on multiple LVLMs and datasets show HardPatch can craft effective adversarial images.

entry.title: EgoUseBench: A benchmark testing computer-use AI agents as first-person context changes
entry.summary: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces EgoUseBench, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents that use first-person observations from devices such as smart glasses to carry out computer tasks. It covers three interaction settings and includes 693 tasks built from over 74 hours of real-world first-person recordings. The authors find that average success rates in the Online Ego Use setting are 26.3% lower than in standard Computer-Use.

entry.title: Benchmark and training method for medical video language models (MedEvidU)
entry.summary: Evidence-Aligned Benchmarking and Learning for Medical Video Language Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper identifies three problems in medical video language models: benchmarks that can be answered without the video, encoders that blend neighboring frames, and models that memorize training questions. It introduces MedEvidU, including MedVidBench-v2, a benchmark of 34 tasks from 18 surgical and clinical video datasets, and label-matched question resampling (LQR). The authors report that these methods raise a 4B model's grounding IoU from 30.4 to 44.4, above a supervised 27B model.

entry.title: SceneDesigner++: A Unified 9-DoF Pose Control Framework for Text-to-Image and Text-to-Video Generation
entry.summary: SceneDesigner++: A Unified 9-DoF Pose Control Framework for T2I and T2V Generation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents SceneDesigner++, a framework that lets users control the 9-DoF pose of objects, covering location, size, and 3D orientation, in both text-to-image and text-to-video generation. It is trained on the authors' ObjectPose9D++ dataset and combines absolute pose encoding with a relative pose encoding called VPRoPE to keep frame-level placement and inter-frame motion coherent. The authors report that it outperforms same-backbone baselines in pose fidelity and motion quality.

entry.title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmark for Proxy-Guided Video Generation
entry.summary: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces ProxyGenBench, a benchmark for evaluating video generation guided by structural proxies such as animated 3D blockouts. It includes 312 evaluation cases from 60 scenes across three scene tasks, with controlled variations in proxy fidelity, text detail, and multimodal inputs. Five video generators were assessed using verified, case-specific checklists. The experiments show that proxies improve spatiotemporal control, but more proxy detail can coincide with poorer completion, and strong structural adherence does not ensure correct binding of conditions to entities and events.

entry.title: Value learning for choosing when to use EEG fusion in human-robot collaboration
entry.summary: Decision-Aligned Value Learning for Selective Adoption of EEG Fusion in Human-Robot Collaboration arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies when EEG signals actually improve predictions in human-robot collaboration. The authors treat selective EEG use as a per-sample incremental value estimation problem and propose VECTA, which separates generating an EEG-informed Fusion prediction from deciding whether it should replace the Base prediction. Cross-subject evaluations on three HRC datasets show that estimated gains track realized gains and that VECTA reduces Brier loss and harmful Fusion adoption under budget constraints.

entry.title: PreserveReward: A Consistency Reward Model for Image Editing Using Dual-Teacher Self-Distillation
entry.summary: PreserveReward: Reliable Consistency Reward Modeling for Image Editing via Dual-Teacher On-Policy Self-Distillation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces PreserveReward, a reward model that evaluates whether image editing preserves content that should remain unchanged. It integrates visual On-Policy Self-Distillation to detect subtle visual changes and judge whether they match the editing intent, using a local teacher with matched crops and a joint teacher with global context. According to the paper, the model aligns strongly with human preferences on non-edited content preservation across multiple benchmarks and generalizes well to diverse editing scenarios.

entry.title: vSFT: Learning to Verbally Tune Agents at Test Time
entry.summary: vSFT: Learning to Verbally Tune Agents at Test Time arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes vSFT, a framework that lets language model agents improve at test time by combining natural-language feedback with weight updates. An agent and a supervisor form a closed loop via a hypernetwork: the supervisor writes verbal feedback on failed trajectories, and the hypernetwork turns that feedback into low-rank weight updates. Using Qwen3-4B, the authors report higher success rates than GRPO and Reflexion on ALFWorld and WebShop.

entry.title: Turning Strong Video Models into Action-Conditioned Robot World Simulators
entry.summary: Most of the Way There: Turning a Strong Video Prior into an Action-Conditioned World Model arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces Dianjing, a lightweight method that adapts a strong video generator so it predicts the physical consequences of specific robot actions rather than just plausible futures. Built on the 33B-parameter MiniMax H3 model, it freezes the backbone and trains only 0.34% of parameters using about 65 hours of robot video from two embodiments. The authors report that it achieves the best scores on four of five tracks in the WorldOracle evaluation.

entry.title: Testing a Small AI Model's Ability to Pull Safety Lessons from Aviation Accident Reports
entry.summary: Evaluating Aviation Safety Knowledge Extraction with SmolLM2: From Zero-Shot to Retrieval-Grounded Prompting arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This study tests SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct, a small language model, on extracting safety knowledge from 300 National Transportation Safety Board aviation accident narratives from 2000 to 2020. It compares zero-shot, one-shot, fixed few-shot, and retrieval-grounded prompting across concept accuracy, verbatim evidence grounding, structural compliance, and directed relation extraction. No single prompting strategy performed best on every measure; retrieval-grounded prompting achieved the highest concept micro-F1 of 32.27%, while directed relation extraction emerged as the main bottleneck.

entry.title: One Representation for Change Detection from Text or Examples
entry.summary: One Representation to Rule Them All -- Open-Vocabulary Change Detection from Text or Visual Examples arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper presents OVTSID3, a training-free framework for open-vocabulary change detection that performs region grouping, concept identification, and temporal comparison in the DINOv3 representation space. Users can specify target changes with zero-shot text queries or one-shot visual prompts using a masked reference pair. It outperforms prior training-free methods on two building and two natural-disaster benchmarks, raising average F1 by 8.9 points. It also achieves state-of-the-art results on SECOND for semantic change detection.

entry.title: Calibrating Human Arm Muscle Models with Differentiable Physics: Ways to Improve Accuracy
entry.summary: Calibration of Neuromusculoskeletal Models Using Differentiable Physics: Recommendations for Improving Model Accuracy arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper compares several modules for calibrating differentiable neuromusculoskeletal (NMS) models on the same upper limb model. The modules include muscle synergy, learnable bone parameters, optimizable wrap object geometry, and constraint torque. Sixteen calibration configurations were tested on nine movements across four subjects, measuring joint torque error. Muscle synergy extrapolation reduced torque loss by 23.6% on average, and bone dynamic parameter optimization reduced it by 10.9%, and both are recommended for calibration.

entry.title: Examining which attention heads in self-supervised speech models detect synthetic speech
entry.summary: A Head-Level Investigative Study of Self-Supervised Backbones for Synthetic Speech Detection arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This study analyzes individual attention heads in two frozen speech models, WavLM-base and Wav2Vec2-base, using the ASVspoof 5 dataset. Only a few heads drive the spoof decision, and removing them lowers equal error rate without retraining, by 13% relative for WavLM and 22% for Wav2Vec2. The authors also find that spoofed speech produces more focused attention than genuine speech, a gap that alone separates the two classes nearly as well as the full representation.

entry.title: Can Visual World Models Sense Force?
entry.summary: Can Visual World Models See Force? arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper asks whether visual world models and vision-language-action policy models, proposed as foundations for robot manipulation, represent the interaction force involved in manipulation. The authors define force awareness as detecting when contact occurs, tracking how force changes, and reflecting its magnitude. They train lightweight readouts on frozen model representations using synchronized video and force data from two manipulation datasets. Most models capture when contact happens but not how much force is applied, and robot post-training does not improve this.

entry.title: DocSEAM: A method that lets models read across page breaks in multi-page documents
entry.summary: DocSEAM: Bidirectional Cross-Page Encoding for Multi-Page Document Understanding arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Vision-language models for multi-page documents currently process each page separately, which breaks context at page boundaries. The paper introduces DocSEAM, a lightweight module placed between a vision encoder and a language model that enriches each page's visual tokens with information from its neighboring pages without changing the token count. The authors report that their 9B-parameter model achieves state-of-the-art results among evaluated open-weight models up to 10B parameters on five multi-page document VQA benchmarks. They also show reduced sensitivity to page boundary placement and better cross-page span localization.

entry.title: SPGSR: A Small Generator for One-Step Image Super-Resolution
entry.summary: SPGSR: A Small Pixel-Space Generator for One-Step Super-Resolution arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces SPGSR, a vision-only one-step super-resolution framework that learns an RGB correction added to the low-resolution image, guided by a frozen DINOv2 and refined locally by a lightweight block. Across three benchmarks it achieves higher PSNR/SSIM and lower LPIPS/DISTS than VOSR, a leading vision-only method. Its generator has 31.8M parameters, about 6.5% the size of VOSR-0.5B. It is also competitive with T2I-based super-resolution methods.

entry.title: CHASE: Curiosity-Guided Skill Acquisition for Robots Executing Embodied Tasks
entry.summary: CHASE: Curiosity-Guided Skill Acquisition for Embodied Task Execution arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how robots working in partially observed environments can form task-relevant hypotheses, seek evidence, and acquire missing skills during execution, inspired by human curiosity. The authors propose CHASE, a framework that treats curiosity as choosing investigations that resolve task uncertainty and expand executable capabilities, linking scene understanding, hypothesis-driven planning, on-demand skill acquisition, and verified execution. Simulation and real-robot experiments report 50-80% task success under combined information and capability gaps, with 70-90% evidence resolution.

entry.title: SemProxy: Semantic 3D Proxies for Steering AI Coding Agents in 3D Modeling
entry.summary: SemProxy: Semantic 3D Proxies for Controllable Agentic 3D Modeling arXiv · Nov 25, 2026SemProxy is a lightweight intermediate representation that uses labeled 3D bounding boxes to let users specify object parts and spatial layouts, while coding agents handle geometric details. The proxies can be serialized into structured text or rendered as images, so existing coding agents can use them without extra training or modification. The authors also present ProxyStudio, an interface combining text, image references, and interactive 3D proxy editing. The paper reports demonstrations on object- and scene-level modeling with different coding agents and a user study on controllable human-agent collaboration.

entry.title: Agentic Waterfall: an intent-driven framework that lets users steer information discovery instead of passive feeds
entry.summary: Agentic Waterfall: An Intent-Driven Information Discovery Framework for Reclaiming User Control in the Attention Economy arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper formalizes a personalized information discovery problem in which users actively direct recommendations and the system adapts to needs inferred from explicit requests and browsing. It proposes the Agentic Waterfall framework, a language-model controller that maintains persistent user state and coordinates retrieval, ranking, and state updates, along with a new dataset and a replay-based evaluation protocol. The framework stays competitive with strong baselines on five public recommendation benchmarks and, on the new dataset, outperforms the strongest baseline in both evaluations, with relative improvements of up to 16.1%.

entry.title: Editing driving policies to keep self-driving cars safe in closed loop
entry.summary: Recoverability policy editing for closed-loop safety in autonomous driving arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper addresses the lack of safety guarantees in neural-network-based autonomous driving. It proposes a state-level policy editing method that ensures closed-loop safety under recoverable disturbances while reusing the model's existing driving capabilities. The method introduces policy recoverability and edits policy outputs only in states that are long-term unsafe but recoverable, resuming the original policy after recovery.
