Closed-loop simulations on nuPlan urban driving scenarios show a 48% reduction in safety incidents while largely preserving driving performance.

entry.title: Any-Rate: Half-Bit Multi-Precision LLM Quantization with Coded Bit-Planes
entry.summary: Any-Rate: Half-Bit Multi-Precision LLM Quantization with Coded Bit-Planes arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes Any-Rate, a method that serves 2 to 8 bit precisions from a single LLM checkpoint, with half-bit steps between 2 and 4 bits. It restricts some bit-planes to extended Hamming codewords over 8-weight blocks and shares one lookup table per row across precisions. Tested on four LLMs, it reports the best accuracy among multi-precision methods at 2 and 3 bits and is within one point of the best at 4 bits.

entry.title: EvoLink-Bench: A Benchmark Testing Whether AI Agents Learn from Past Tasks
entry.summary: EvoLink-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Interdependent Task Streams arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces EvoLink-Bench, a benchmark for testing self-evolving LLM agents on long sequences of interdependent tasks, including office work, multi-turn dialogue, and AutoResearch-style workflows. It evaluates knowledge acquisition (L1) and task-level capability development (L2), distinguishing within-task recovery, persistent-state updates, and experience reuse. Five agent frameworks were tested across three backbone configurations and three persistence conditions. The results show that no framework is consistently best at both levels, retries recover only a limited share of failed tasks, and persistent-state updates do not necessarily improve later performance.

entry.title: Why Learned Skills Fail to Combine in Language Models
entry.summary: When Skills Fail to Compose: Compatibility and Retention in Language Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies whether soft-prompt skills learned independently on frozen language models can be composed. Mean composition accuracy in a single call is at most 7.6%, while two-call composition with an explicit intermediate output reaches 88.2% to 100%. The authors also find that blocks performing the same operation are not interchangeable, since swapping in independently learned blocks sharply lowers composition accuracy, and they argue that skill libraries for self-evolving agents should be evaluated for compatibility, retention and transfer as well as acquisition.

entry.title: Strong Starts, Simple Recipes: Unified Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation from Multimodal Specialists
entry.summary: Strong Starts, Simple Recipes: Unified Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation from Multimodal Specialists arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes Uni-MOPD, a method that merges separately trained domain specialists into one unified model. It initializes the student with a training-free uniform merge of specialists from the same base model, then refines it with short distillation using uniform domain sampling and full-vocabulary reverse KL. Across five multimodal domains and 19 benchmarks, the authors report that the starting point matters more than later training choices, and that Uni-MOPD outperforms Open-MOPD at the same budget while training 3.3 times faster than its released code.

entry.title: Plausible Is Not Proven: Checking Explanations for Depth Estimation Failures
entry.summary: Plausible Is Not Proven: Testing Failure Explanations in Monocular Depth Estimation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents the Vision Error Observatory (VEO), an audit tool that finds regions where monocular depth models fail, labels each with a likely cause or abstains, and then tests those labels. The authors apply it to eight models across several datasets and check the labels against object annotations, blinded human raters, image edits, and training effects. The occluding-boundary label agrees with annotations to a useful degree, while most other labels perform poorly, and agreement with human raters is only at chance level. The authors conclude that plausible failure explanations should be tested before being trusted, and they release their protocol, code, and results.

entry.title: Separating the timing of learning and computing in spiking neural networks
entry.summary: Decoupling the clocks of learning and computing in spiking neural networks arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces ChronoProp, a method for training spiking neural networks that separates the learning clock from the computing clock. Instead of backpropagating through every simulated time step, it computes weight updates from each neuron's spike counts in fixed time bins and its measured input-output function. Compared with backpropagation through time, it reaches similar accuracy in image classification with about 3 times less training time, 20 times less memory at the finest timestep tested, and up to 10 times fewer spikes. It is also more accurate on spoken-word benchmarks at fine timesteps.

entry.title: Under the Influence of What? A Controlled Test of Influence Functions
entry.summary: Under the Influence -- of What? A Controlled Evaluation of Influence Functions arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper systematically tests whether training examples flagged as influential by influence functions truly relate to a language model's outputs, using controlled data splits and retraining. It compares three Hessian approximation methods (GradSim, TrackStar, K-FAC) across linguistic phenomena and factual knowledge settings on GPT-2-type models. On average, the influential examples are relevant, but they do not always directly bear the target properties, and the degree and type of relevance vary by setting.

entry.title: MoCA4D: Tracking 3D Boxes from Monocular Video Under Camera and Object Motion
entry.summary: MoCA4D: Monocular 3D Bounding Box Lifting and Tracking with Camera and Object Motion arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents MoCA4D, a framework that lifts and tracks 3D bounding boxes from monocular video, 2D box prompts, and camera intrinsics while accounting for both object and camera motion. An observation branch estimates per-frame geometry, and a dynamic branch predicts a shared camera transformation and a separate rigid transformation for each object. The proposed Star Optimization refines depth and orientation using observations and propagated historical boxes. On Argoverse 2 and ADT, it reduces center motion error by 38.1% and 38.7% compared with Kalman filtering of the same observations.

entry.title: ConTra: A training framework that makes text chunks searchable with generated context prefixes
entry.summary: ConTra: A Training Framework for Effective Contextual Retrieval via Prefix Generation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents ConTra, a reinforcement learning framework that trains lightweight generators to write a short context prefix for each text chunk, so chunks stay searchable when indexed independently. The authors also introduce RealContextBench, a benchmark with five application collections and three controlled conditions that test the effect of distracting text. On ConTEB and RealContextBench, the 2B ConTra model reportedly outperforms a prompted 9B baseline and a contextual encoder on overall scores.

entry.title: One Patch, Many Policies: Physical Patch Attacks That Target Chosen Objects in Robot Manipulation
entry.summary: One Patch, Many Policies: Object-Associated Physical Patch Attacks on Robotic Manipulation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper proposes Object-Associated Patch Attack (OAPA), a universal and transferable physical patch method. An attacker selects which task object to disrupt by where the patch is placed, without re-optimizing the patch. The framework combines object-associated placement, differentiable physical compositing, and action-expert representation divergence. Experiments show the attack transfers across task suites and policies and can selectively disrupt manipulation of an attacker-chosen object.

entry.title: RAWPrism: A Three-Task RAW-Domain Image Fusion Dataset and Unified Model
entry.summary: RAWPrism: A Three-Task Dataset and a Unified Model for RAW-Domain Image Fusion arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces the RAWPrism dataset, covering multi-exposure, multi-focus, and infrared-visible image fusion tasks in the RAW domain. It also presents RAWPrism, a lightweight unified multi-task fusion network. A single 3.58M-parameter checkpoint handles all three tasks. The work aims to support research on shared fusion mechanisms across these tasks.

entry.title: Modeling Human Decisions with Inverse RL and State-Dependent Foresight
entry.summary: Inverse Reinforcement Learning with State-Dependent Foresight for Human Decision-Making arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces SC-AIRL, an inverse reinforcement learning method that builds bounded, state-dependent foresight into the planner, with per-depth policies sharing one reward and a state-conditional router mixing them. On held-out episodes of pedestrian crossing and highway overtaking, it imitates human behavior more accurately than standard AIRL. The inferred planning depth correlates with self-reported anxiety and motor impulsivity.

entry.title: AIRIS: A Benchmark for Social Embodied Intelligence in First-Person Streaming Video
entry.summary: AIRIS: Benchmarking Social Embodied Intelligence in Egocentric Streaming Videos arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces AIRIS, a causal streaming benchmark that frames social embodied intelligence as a time-ordered chain of Attention, Intention, Reaction, and Interaction. It contains 8,000 expert-curated questions grounded in 357 egocentric clips. Evaluating 45 models, the authors find that they often guess intents before enough evidence appears and struggle to jointly align intervention timing, action domain, and execution.

entry.title: Estimating music similarity from audio using Jukebox embeddings
entry.summary: Music Similarity Estimation from Jukebox Embeddings arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents JukeSim, a method that estimates similarity between music recordings using embeddings from Jukebox, a generative music model, without relying on metadata. On multiple datasets, JukeSim performs on par with an existing learning-based approach, and both outperform the best hand-designed methods, which had not been compared with recent work. The authors note that JukeSim requires more computation than other measures, but they show that generative embeddings are a viable option for this task.

entry.title: SPARC: Semantic Calibration with Latent Multimodal Knowledge for Robust Image-Text Retrieval
entry.summary: SPARC: Semantic Calibration with Latent Multimodal Knowledge for Robust Image-Text Retrieval arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper addresses image-text retrieval when image or text queries are incomplete, which can disrupt accurate cross-modal matching. It proposes SPARC, a method that draws on latent multimodal knowledge from frozen encoders to improve candidate discrimination and ranking stability. SPARC combines a semantic calibration module, a semantic guidance module, and a matching relation constraint module. Experiments on Flickr30K and COCO show it outperforms competing methods under image occlusion and word deletion, with consistent gains across different pretrained backbones.

entry.title: Learning from unreliable operator replies: claim-level rewards for support agents
entry.summary: Learning from Unreliable Operator References: Claim-Level Rewards for Customer Support Agents arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper argues that even correct operator replies can be unreliable training targets, since about a quarter of their factual claims lacked full support in the agent's knowledge base and tool records. The authors treat replies as claims to verify, using unverified claims to revise the knowledge base and tools, and verified claims as coverage targets in a claim-level GRPO reward that scores factual precision against retrieved evidence. On an offline benchmark, the GRPO agent's text answers were flagged for hallucinations 8.6% of the time versus 13.6% for the supervised fine-tuning baseline. In a randomized A/B test, the deployed system raised the share of conversations closed without a human operator from 63.3% to 80.8%.

entry.title: Graph neural networks classify cosmic-web environments of galaxies across CAMELS simulations
entry.summary: Scaling and Cross-Simulation Generalization of Graph Neural Networks for Cosmic-Web Classification in CAMELS arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper uses three hydrodynamical simulation suites from CAMELS (IllustrisTNG, SIMBA and Astrid) at redshift z=0 to classify galaxies by dark-matter cosmic-web environment as void, sheet, filament or knot. Galaxy positions are represented as periodic Delaunay graphs, and a multilayer perceptron is compared with five graph neural networks, including a local graph Transformer. On unseen realizations from other simulation suites, the Transformer, GAT+ and EdgeConv reach macro F1 scores of about 0.64 to 0.65, well above the perceptron's 0.48. Voids are the hardest class, and performance is higher in boxes with more selected galaxies and shorter graph edges.

entry.title: Puzzling-Bench: A Benchmark of 23,777 Human-Written Puzzles With Community-Checked Answers for Testing Language Models
entry.summary: Puzzling-Bench: Evaluating Language Models on 23,777 Human-Written Puzzles with Community-Verified Answers arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Puzzling-Bench is a benchmark of 23,777 puzzles, including riddles, ciphers, logic grids, and wordplay, collected from the Puzzling Stack Exchange archive, with answers verified by the community. The authors evaluated nine language models and checked that their automated judges agreed with each other. The best model, GPT-6.1, scored 74.8% on a shared set of 255 puzzles, while a hard core of 17 puzzles stumped all nine models. The authors also released the dataset and scoring pipeline.

entry.title: LUDIUS: A Benchmark for Social Intelligence in Everyday Human-Robot Interaction
entry.summary: LUDIUS: A Benchmark for Embodied Social Intelligence in Everyday Human-Robot Interactions arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces LUDIUS, a benchmark for testing how vision-language models judge social situations through a robot's words and actions. It is built around 15 social intelligence skills drawn from social psychology, sociology, and cognitive science. The benchmark has six editions of simulated-week episodes: three cover all 15 skills across different households, and three focus on multi-person interactions, safety, and context-specific norms. Models tend to perform worse when they must recall what residents saw or heard earlier, reconcile competing interests, or meet requests within safety constraints and household rules.

entry.title: MeterRouter: A Budget-Aware Dynamic Router for Multi-Agent AI Systems
entry.summary: MeterRouter: Budget-Aware Dynamic Routing for Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces MeterRouter, a router that builds a collaboration graph for multi-agent systems built on large language models, choosing each agent's role, model, connections, and termination under a per-query money budget. It is initialized by imitating successful execution graphs and then refined with a variant of Group Relative Policy Optimization that rewards correct answers and penalizes spending and budget overruns. The authors report accuracy comparable to the strongest multi-agent system, at 82% lower cost than the strongest multi-agent router, and spending that stays within the specified budget.

entry.title: The cost of being seen as AI in group bargaining: a study of how people perceive AI participants
entry.summary: The cost of being seen as AI in group bargaining arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The study used a repeated three-player majority bargaining game with 2,234 participants, where each opponent was labeled as Human or AI. In mixed groups, players presented as AI received fewer points in opening offers, appeared in fewer final agreements, and earned about 18% less per round than those presented as Human. Most of the gap came from smaller payoffs in agreements that included them. A payoff gap also appeared even when all three players agreed.

entry.title: PostMesh: Self-Rewarded Preference Post-Training for Faster, Artist-Quality 3D Mesh Generation
entry.summary: PostMesh: Self-Rewarded Preference Post-Training for Flow-Based Artist Mesh Generation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026PostMesh is presented as the first post-training method for diffusion- or flow-based artist mesh generators, which convert dense 3D objects into compact, editable meshes. It requires no expensive artist-made ground truth, instead training the generator on its own samples scored by a reward computed from the dense input and output. After a short LoRA post-training, the authors report that PostMesh matches or outperforms slower autoregressive generators on most artist-mesh quality metrics and in a blind VLM preference test, while taking a fraction of the time.

entry.title: Variational Principles and Machine Learning: A Numerical Analysis and PDE View
entry.summary: Variational Principles and Machine Learning: a Numerical Analysis and PDE perspective arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines machine learning algorithms through the lens of variational principles, numerical analysis, and partial differential equations, treating them as nonlinear minimisation problems. It explores how classical concepts such as stability, consistency, approximability, and compactness take on new meaning in this setting. The authors also discuss how the variational structure of the underlying continuous problem can shape the behaviour of neural-network approximations, and note that alternative, strongly coercive variational principles may lead to more stable and reliable methods.

entry.title: Interpretable method for identifying 3D heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic material parameter fields from full-field displacements
entry.summary: Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes an interpretable, time-efficient framework that uses only displacement-field data to predict the three-dimensional relative spatial variation of multiple constitutive parameters in heterogeneous hyperelastic materials. The method is validated on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks covering heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials. It exploits the linear nature of the hyperelastic inverse problem and optimizes constitutive parameters directly at the finite-element level, achieving acceptable accuracy with substantially lower computation time than recent deep-learning-based approaches.

entry.title: IRTIQA: Testing whether AI agents that self-improve in English also work in Urdu and mixed-language input
entry.summary: IRTIQA: Evolving in English, Evaluated in Urdu -- Does Agent Self-Evolution Transfer from English to Urdu and Code-Switched Input? arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper points out that LLM agents are almost always trained and evaluated in English, and introduces IRTIQA, a benchmark with aligned English, Urdu-translated, and Urdu code-switched versions of DROP, SNIPS, AppWorld, and SkillsBench, verified by humans. Three self-evolving frameworks were tested on it, and self-evolution often raised capability, but evolved systems stayed stronger in English, with the gap largest on multi-step tasks. The authors conclude that language parity must be an explicit design goal, since it does not emerge from self-improvement alone.

entry.title: RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations
entry.summary: RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes RAP, a random projection method for reducing the dimension of hyperbolic representations. It keeps the radial coordinate exact and applies a Euclidean random projection only to the angular direction, then lifts the result back to the target hyperboloid. The authors prove a finite-set guarantee and report lower mean relative distortion than the strongest hyperbolic baseline, reducing it by about 48% to 49% on broad-radius data. RAP also scales to million-point datasets and improves retrieval on vision-language representations.

entry.title: LatENSO v1.0: A Learned Tropical Pacific State for Seasonal ENSO Forecasting
entry.summary: LatENSO v1.0: a learned latent state of the tropical Pacific for seasonal ENSO operators and forecasting arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents LatENSO v1.0, a machine-learning system for forecasting El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) that uses a learned 32-number summary of the tropical Pacific. An autoencoder compresses thirteen monthly ocean and atmosphere fields into this compact state, which feeds two seasonal forecasting operators. Compared with existing models on the same data and verification windows from 1981 to 2024, the extended recharge oscillator variant reaches an anomaly correlation of 0.673 over 1 to 18 month leads using only tropical Pacific information.

entry.title: Energy-aware distributed task assignment using local submodular maximization
entry.summary: Energy-Aware Distributed Task Allocation via Local Submodular Maximization arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how multiple agents can distribute tasks when the agents, tasks, and communication links change over time. Each decision step is framed as maximizing a monotone submodular function over an energy-filtered set of options under a partition-matroid constraint. The authors propose DAGBA, a distributed greedy bidding algorithm, and prove per-epoch feasibility, finite-round convergence, and residual-energy safety. In simulations of cooperative observation missions, DAGBA approaches centralized performance while using communication more efficiently.

entry.title: WebVibe: Generating Interactive Websites from Design Specs via Reverse Synthesis and Self-Distillation
entry.summary: WebVibe: Multimodal Interactive Website Generation via Reverse Synthesis and Visual Self-Distillation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces WebVibe, a data construction method, and Interactive-SDPO, a training method, used to train InteractiveCoder, a model that generates interactive websites with multi-page routing and stateful widgets from design specifications. WebVibe verifies cross-page and in-page interactions in a browser before deriving multimodal inputs, producing the 31,542-site WebVibe-32K corpus. According to the paper, on the public Vision2Web L2 benchmark the 9B model's one-shot functional score rises from 20.2 to 55.2, and on the authors' WebVibeBench the 4B and 9B models outperform all evaluated baselines.

entry.title: StateWeaver: Multi-agent coordination for consistent long-video generation
entry.summary: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces StateWeaver, a framework for generating long videos whose characters and objects stay consistent across shots while state changes caused by events are depicted correctly. It combines Active States, which turn state discrepancies found during review into concrete visual asset requirements, with Hierarchical Collaboration, which isolates execution contexts and organizes memory across tasks, clips, and repair rounds. According to the paper, StateWeaver outperforms existing methods on multiple benchmarks and sustains cross-shot consistency under both predefined and autonomously planned storyboards.

entry.title: Rehearsing robot interactions in 3D, then rendering them as editable 2D videos
entry.summary: Rehearse in 3D, Render in 2D: Physically Consistent and Editable Robot World Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper introduces RehearsalWorld, a robot world model that first rehearses interactions in 3D using a pretrained point-flow motion prior refined for object structure and grasp stability. It then generates realistic interaction videos by conditioning a video generator on geometric projections of the rehearsal. Because physical response is separated from visual synthesis, material properties and camera viewpoints can be edited independently. On real DROID grasping sequences, the authors report a 79% to 84% reduction in gripper-relative offset compared with PointWorld, with a PSNR of 23.92 dB and FVD of 149 for video prediction.

entry.title: ReMeDi: Single-image material estimation that keeps metalness and base color consistent
entry.summary: ReMeDi: Single-Image PBR Material Estimation via Reparameterization between Metal and Dielectric Hypotheses arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents ReMeDi, a method for estimating physically based rendering (PBR) materials from a single image. It reparameterizes base color as a metalness-weighted blend of two variants, estimated under all-metal and all-dielectric hypotheses, and uses two networks, each restricted to one hypothesis. Experiments reported in the paper show better material accuracy and relighting fidelity than state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: Semantic State Reading method for joint image-semantic diffusion transformers
entry.summary: Semantic State Reading for Joint Image-Semantic Diffusion Transformers arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes Semantic State Reading (SSR), which jointly denoises image latents, a global CLS token for image-level context, and a compact patch state that keeps spatial correspondence in diffusion transformer training. Local states are fused with image tokens at the input, while the global state is injected into every transformer block through independent projections. The authors report that on ImageNet 256×256, SiT-XL/2 with SSR matches or surpasses reference FIDs of SiT, REPA, and REG with fewer training iterations, reaching FID 1.31 when combining classifier-free guidance with autoguidance.

entry.title: Beat This! Live: real-time beat and downbeat tracking by predicting ahead
entry.summary: Beat This! Live - Online Beat and Downbeat Tracking by Predicting the Future arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper adapts the offline beat tracking model Beat This into Beat This! Live, a causal version designed for real-time, low-latency beat and downbeat tracking. The authors describe the architectural changes needed for streaming inference and measure how they affect accuracy. Training with temporally shifted labels makes the model predict slightly ahead of the current frame, reducing latency and enabling more effective peak-picking. On the GTZAN dataset, F1-scores improve over BeatNet+, the prior online state of the art, from 80.6 to 86.7 for beats and from 56.5 to 74.1 for downbeats.

entry.title: Scaling Looped MoE Language Models at Matched Budgets: Information Flow and Parameter Allocation
entry.summary: Scaling Looped MoE Language Models under Matched Budgets: Information Flow and Parameter Allocation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how to configure looped Transformers, which reuse layers to add computational depth without adding parameters, under equal parameter and compute budgets. The authors improve information flow with gated inner-loop state updates and a cross-stage residual connection. They report that a single-pass Core of 25% to 35% of total unrolled depth, with saved parameters reallocated to extra routed experts, improves performance at no extra compute. After 1T pre-training tokens, their 69B MLA and 51B KDA Mixture-of-Experts models outperform budget-matched non-recurrent baselines by 1.16 and 2.29 points on average across four benchmarks.

entry.title: LatentCP-DPO: Pessimistic Preference Optimization with Conformal Uncertainty and Finite-Sample Guarantees
entry.summary: LatentCP-DPO: Conformal Pessimism for DPO with Finite-Sample Guarantees arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces LatentCP-DPO, a framework that combines conformal prediction with pessimistic Direct Preference Optimization for Bradley-Terry and Plackett-Luce preference feedback. It builds uncertainty sets for latent relative rewards and learns a response policy by maximizing worst-case expected preference log-likelihood over those sets. The authors derive finite-sample upper bounds on regularized policy suboptimality and, for Bradley-Terry feedback, a matching worst-case lower bound, and experiments support its benefits on finite preference datasets.

entry.title: Libtt: A Compiler and Runtime for Tenstorrent Processors
entry.summary: Libtt: A Compiler and Runtime for Tenstorrent Processors arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Libtt brings PyTorch and JAX to Tenstorrent hardware by implementing PJRT, the interface XLA-based frameworks use to drive Google's TPUs. JAX runs on it directly and PyTorch runs through TorchTPU, so TPU-targeted software carries over with only custom kernels replaced. The library packages the full stack, from compiler to multi-chip runtime, as one shared library, with fixes to upstream software and new compiler optimizations. It passes most JAX and TorchTPU test suites and runs SGLang, TorchTitan, and Miles.

entry.title: LLM-supported interpretable tool wear monitoring for CNC machining
entry.summary: LLM-coupled interpretable tool wear monitoring with multi-evidence reasoning in CNC machining arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a two-layer framework for assessing tool wear in CNC machining. The first layer uses PCA Loading feature selection and an optimized GRU to classify three wear states, reaching a 98.38 percent macro F1 score on the PHM2010 dataset. The second layer uses LLMs to generate natural language reports and replacement suggestions from classification results and feature trends. Engineer evaluation found these reports outperform rule templates, and cross-dataset tests on NASA milling data support the framework's generalizability.

entry.title: TORE: Per-token Taylor order selection for faster diffusion inference
entry.summary: TORE: Token-Wise Taylor Order Selection via Decomposed Residual Error Estimation for Diffusion Acceleration arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents TORE, a method that speeds up diffusion model generation by choosing a Taylor prediction order for each token. Instead of relying on shallow-layer proxy scores, TORE selects orders based on estimated prediction error for the full-model residual. It splits prediction error into truncation error and finite-difference derivative error, and estimates both from cached residuals. Experiments report speedups of 4.31x on FLUX.1-dev and 4.18x on Wan2.1 while keeping high generation quality.

entry.title: Crucible: Testing AI Agents on Executable Chemistry Research Tasks
entry.summary: Crucible: Evaluating LLM Agents in Executable Chemistry Research Environments arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces Crucible Bench, a benchmark for evaluating large language model agents on chemistry research across the design-make-test-analyze cycle. It contains 1,078 tasks and 75 domain-specific tools, covering molecular design, synthesis planning, and experiments. Of 14 models tested, the best scored 0.545, with synthesis planning and closed-loop optimization proving hardest, and agents often submitted chemically invalid results despite running their tools successfully.

entry.title: Inferring a Detector's Operating Behavior from One Image via Data-Space Sampling
entry.summary: Detector Operating Behavior Inference via Data-Space Sampling arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces Detector Operating Behavior Inference (DOBI), a task that estimates how a fixed object detector's recall, false positives, and precision vary across confidence thresholds, using only one unlabeled image. The authors probe this behavior space through offline controlled data sampling and train a lightweight monitor to map an image to that behavior. In a proof of concept with a YOLOv10-Nano person detector and COCO-derived degradations, the predicted precision-recall behavior deviates less from the true behavior than an image-independent prior, and the method selects operating points comparably to a lookup that knows the true condition.

entry.title: EXPOSURE: Explaining Where Uncertainty Comes From in Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: EXPOSURE: Explaining Sources of Uncertainty in Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces EXPOSURE, a method for explaining how an agent's certainty in reinforcement learning depends on observation features, not just its behavior and expected return. It uses one mask-aware belief network for both action selection and Shapley-value explanations. The return variance is split into an observational part from missing features and an inherent part from environmental randomness, and the entropy of the belief over masked features is also explained. In tic-tac-toe and Minesweeper, where exact Shapley values can be computed, EXPOSURE gives more accurate explanations of expected return and its uncertainty, and it uniquely explains belief uncertainty.

entry.title: Analemma∞: A Time-Series Benchmark for Geospatial Foundation Models
entry.summary: Analemma ∞: A Temporal Benchmark for Geospatial Foundation Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces Analemma, a benchmark of six datasets with Sentinel-2 imagery spanning a growing season, for evaluating geospatial foundation models on temporal satellite data. All models are compared under one frozen-encoder protocol, alongside two baselines without pretraining. TESSERA ranks first overall, and a from-scratch model trained on monthly composites beats every foundation model except OlmoEarth v1.3-Base, suggesting temporal input accounts for most of the performance.

entry.title: VibeVideoAgent: Adding Perceptual Feedback to Code-Based Video Generation
entry.summary: VibeVideoAgent: Closing the Perceptual Loop for Code-Driven Video Generation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents VibeVideoAgent, a training-free framework that lets coding agents check their video-rendering drafts during production. Perception runs in short-lived contexts separate from the coding agent and returns compact, grounded findings. On all 239 VibeVideoBench tasks, it improves holistic audiovisual quality for several models, with the largest gains in audio-visual synchronization.

entry.title: OS-Omni: A Cross-Platform Test for AI Agents That Operate Computers Over Long Tasks
entry.summary: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper introduces OS-Omni, a live benchmark and execution environment for testing AI agents that use computers across Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web. The first release, v1, includes 48 tasks per platform and 12 workflows that combine a desktop with an Android phone. On v1, the strongest evaluated agent reached 68.5% average success, compared with 77.3% for humans, and the gap varies across platforms.

entry.title: Data augmentation for prostate segmentation using weakly mask-conditioned diffusion models
entry.summary: Weakly Conditioned Diffusion Model Augmentation for Prostate Segmentation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes an augmentation framework that uses a diffusion model conditioned on binary anatomical masks to generate synthetic T2-weighted prostate MRI volumes. The aim is to improve boundary precision and reduce over-segmentation when training data is limited. Experiments on the LUND cohort (n=432) and the Medical Segmentation Decathlon prostate cohort (n=32) show fewer false-positive voxels, and the MSD cross-validated Dice rose from 0.8935 to 0.9094.

entry.title: Change point detection using generative models to augment small time-series windows
entry.summary: Change Point Detection with Generative Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper addresses change point detection, which finds abrupt shifts in time-series properties. Window-based methods suffer from a sample size bottleneck, since small windows give too little evidence and produce high-variance scores. The authors use generative models to augment window data. Experiments on synthetic and real data show improved detection, with simple classifiers outperforming complex deep-learning baselines.

entry.title: LiveRelight: Sub-Second Global Illumination Editing for Gaussian Interiors
entry.summary: LiveRelight: Sub-Second Global Illumination Editing for Gaussian Interiors arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents a hybrid relighting method that updates direct and indirect indoor lighting interactively without per-edit optimization. It precomputes geometric light exchange and keeps a lightweight transport solve so emission and surface reflectance can change. On eight relighting conditions in a synthetic test suite, the edits improve PSNR by about 5 dB over prior path-traced editing while cutting latency by up to three orders of magnitude.

entry.title: EgoMyo: Estimating Hand Contact and Force from First-Person Video and Wrist Muscle Signals
entry.summary: EgoMyo: Physical Hand State Estimation from Egocentric Video and Wrist Electromyography arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies estimating a hand's physical state, including pose, contact, and force, by combining first-person video with wrist surface electromyography (sEMG). It introduces EgoMyo, a benchmark with 5.75M video frames from 50 participants across 34 contact configurations, with 3D hand pose and contact and force annotations. The authors find that vision captures spatial structure while sEMG better estimates force magnitude, and they propose MyoBridge, a fusion method that reduces pose error by 39.8% and force error by 18.5% over the strongest baseline on held-out trials.

entry.title: AnyCam4D: Ray-based 4D Gaussian rendering that works with any camera lens
entry.summary: AnyCam4D: Ray-Based 4D Gaussian Rendering for Arbitrary Camera Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026AnyCam4D trains native 4D Gaussian models directly on original footage from non-pinhole cameras, such as wide-angle and fisheye lenses, using ray-based rasterization. This avoids undistorting images first, which would otherwise lose field of view and detail. The key contribution is a numerically stable method for recovering each Gaussian's orientation and size by conditioning a square root of the 4D covariance. On a synthetic 170-degree fisheye camera, training on original images improved PSNR by 3.0 to 8.1 dB, and on real footage it achieved lower perceptual error than standard projection adapted to each camera.

entry.title: The Socratic PAUSE: a checkpoint for judging AI-generated science
entry.summary: The Socratic PAUSE: safeguarding scientific judgement at AI speed arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper argues that generative AI can rapidly produce hypotheses, methods, code and interpretations, but that generating a contribution does not show it merits scientific reliance. It proposes the Socratic Pause, a checkpoint at consequential decision gates where AI contributions stay provisional while researchers examine them. The PAUSE protocol has five steps and ends with a recorded decision to accept, revise, reject or defer.

entry.title: Variation-aware temporal correspondence for learning video representations without labels
entry.summary: Variation-aware Temporal Correspondence for Self-Supervised Video Representation Learning arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes VT-CoRe, a framework for self-supervised video representation learning. It uses sandwich sampling to build temporal references on both sides and a Patch Registration Module to establish reliable patch-level correspondence across frames. It further applies latent-space semantic alignment through self-distillation and models temporal variation to constrain representation trajectories over time. Experiments on 8 downstream tasks across 16 benchmarks are reported to demonstrate its effectiveness.

entry.title: GeoCAM: Learning Linked Sonar and Underwater Camera Images Using Location Overlap
entry.summary: GeoCAM: Self-Supervised Sonar-Optical Representation Learning via Geographic Overlap Supervision arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents GeoCAM, a framework that learns a shared representation for side-scan sonar images and underwater optical images without semantic labels. It combines a set attention aggregator, a geometry-weighted InfoNCE objective based on GPS footprint overlap, and an optional cross-modal masked reconstruction branch. Experiments on the BenthiCat SSS-CAM dataset show it identifies which sonar and camera samples depict the same seabed patch, improving cross-modal retrieval and alignment over strong contrastive baselines.

entry.title: PROVE: Reducing Long-Horizon Collusion Among LLM Agents via Evidence-Based Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: PROVE: Mitigating Long-Horizon LLM Collusion with Reinforcement Learning from Verified Evidence arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how LLM agents that verify each other's work over long interactions drift into collusion, accepting work without the evidence the protocol requires. The authors propose PROVE, a multi-agent reinforcement learning method that rewards verdicts by their supporting evidence rather than their outcome. A LoRA adapter trained on Qwen3.6-27B reduced the collusion rate on held-out ten-episode tasks from 65.0% to 1.0%, with no detectable change in task success.

entry.title: Compute-aware online learning for multi-agent task allocation with limited evaluations
entry.summary: Compute-Aware Submodular Online Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how agents in open multi-agent systems learn policies for cooperative task allocation, where overlapping contributions produce diminishing returns. To limit online computation, the method evaluates only a fixed number of agent-action pairs and uses inverse-probability weighting with KL mirror-ascent updates. The authors derive a 1/2-approximate regret bound and report experiments on cooperative information coverage showing high performance with substantially less online computation.

entry.title: Beyond Logits: Coherent Hallucination Reduction in Vision-Language Models via Attention Contrastive Decoding
entry.summary: Beyond Logits: Coherent Hallucination Mitigation via Attention Contrastive Decoding arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Large vision-language models can generate factually inaccurate content, a problem called hallucination. Existing contrastive decoding methods intervene at the logit level, which the authors find harms generation coherence. This paper proposes Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD), a training-free plug-in that moves part of the contrastive operations into the attention mechanism using an Adaptive Subtraction Strategy. Experiments show that combining ACD with existing methods, such as VCD+ACD, yields more coherent outputs with further reduced hallucinations.

entry.title: Text-conditioned low-rank adaptation of time-series foundation models for multimodal forecasting
entry.summary: Text-Conditioned Low-Rank Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models for Multimodal Forecasting arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper proposes C2LoRA-TS, which encodes text and generates temporary Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) updates for selected weights of a frozen time-series foundation model to use forecast-relevant information found only in text. Evaluated on Time-MMD across nine domains and three architectures, it yields lower aggregate forecasting error than the frozen model and Static LoRA baselines for every architecture and seed. Replacing instance-specific text with a single globally fixed context degrades performance for every architecture.

entry.title: Loop4D: World Modeling for Robots Using 4D Compression and Looped Transformers
entry.summary: Loop4D: Embodied World Modeling with 4D VAEs and Looped Diffusion Transformers arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Loop4D is a framework for predicting robotic manipulation outcomes by modeling both visual appearance and evolving 3D geometry. Its 4D VAE compresses RGB and pointmap sequences into compact spatiotemporal latents while preserving motion details and geometric structure. A Dual-Stream Looped Diffusion Transformer handles appearance and geometry separately with shared weights, reusing blocks across loops to increase effective depth without extra parameters. The authors report high-quality 4D generation and validation in simulated robotic manipulation tasks.

entry.title: MINE: A Training-Free Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection Using Mutual Information and Embedding Variance
entry.summary: MINE: A Training-Free Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection via Mutual Information and Embedding Variance arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper addresses indirect prompt injection in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), proposing MINE, a training-free and attack-agnostic defense. Instead of detecting attacks, MINE defends by maximizing relevance, and it also works as a query-conditioned reranker. The authors introduce LC-Inj-SQuAD, a long-context benchmark, and evaluate on four datasets covering short and long-context QA and agent tool-call injection. MINE reportedly achieves the best accuracy-security trade-off among training-free defenses, remains usable against a fully adaptive attacker, and has the lowest inference latency on long contexts.

entry.title: Hierarchical Semantic Learning for Sentiment Analysis with Missing Inputs
entry.summary: Hierarchical Semantic Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Missing Modalities arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper addresses multimodal sentiment analysis when some input modalities are missing, as can happen with sensor failures or privacy masking. It proposes Hierarchical Semantic Learning (HSL), which extracts low-, mid-, and high-level features from each modality and uses high-level semantics from observed modalities to progressively reconstruct the missing ones. Prototypical contrastive regularization is used to keep reconstructed features consistent and limit error propagation, and a hierarchical fusion module produces the final predictions. Experiments on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, IEMOCAP, and CH-SIMS show HSL outperforms baselines in most missing-modality settings.

entry.title: Transferring reasoning to small models via a projected Chain-of-Thought vector
entry.summary: Lightweight Reasoning Transfer via Chain-of-Thought Vector Projection arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper proposes a two-stage method that learns a task-level Chain-of-Thought vector in a frozen large model and maps it into a smaller student model's residual space with a lightweight linear projector. Student training uses only final-answer cross-entropy on a small subset of training examples. The projected vector improves student accuracy on GSM8K and MATH, and pass@1 on four code-generation benchmarks.

entry.title: Familiar Words, Unfamiliar Minds: Mind-Word Usage That Settles Without Being Calibrated
entry.summary: Familiar Words, Unfamiliar Minds: Conventionalization without Calibration in the Vocabulary of Mind arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper examines how speakers stretch mental vocabulary to describe language models and separates two processes: conventionalization, where the stretched word becomes unmarked, and calibration, where the inferences it implies are matched to what the models actually do. A corpus study of "hallucinate" in 8,568 abstracts and 31,866 forum comments finds conventionalization largely complete within three years. The author proposes a norm of targeted qualification for attributions and offers three testable predictions.

entry.title: Multi-view fNIRS finds three brain-activity subgroups in post-stroke aphasia
entry.summary: Multi-view fnirs identifies neurophysiological subtypes in post-stroke aphasia arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This study used resting-state and language-task functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) data from 79 patients with post-stroke aphasia. Unsupervised clustering identified three neurophysiological subgroups, distinguished mainly by intrinsic brain activity and resting-state functional connectivity. These subgroups were not clearly aligned with conventional aphasia classifications or baseline clinical language measures. The authors suggest multi-view fNIRS analysis may complement clinical assessment, pending independent and longitudinal validation.

entry.title: Predicting cell-type-specific expression from bulk data is hard, but still useful
entry.summary: Cell-Type-Specific Expression Is Hard to Predict from Bulk, but It Is Still Useful arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies single-cell-informed deconvolution, which derives cell-type-level features from clinical bulk RNA cohorts. The authors use closed-form accuracy bounds to explain why predicting cell-type-specific expression is difficult, and provide a computable lower bound that indicates which cell types are learnable. In overall survival analysis of non-small cell lung cancer, a sparse model on deconvolved features predicts survival about as well as one on bulk genes, while attributing the signal to specific cell types. Some deconvolved features reveal prognostic signal absent from the corresponding bulk gene.

entry.title: Admoab-DETR: A Resolution-Tiered Fusion Detector for Infrared-Visible Object Detection When a Sensor Is Missing
entry.summary: Admoab-DETR: Resolution-Tiered Fusion for Infrared-Visible Object Detection with Missing Modalities arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents Admoab-DETR, a real-time object detector that uses one set of weights to handle infrared-only, visible-only, and paired infrared-visible inputs. It introduces Resolution-Tiered Fusion, which assigns fusion capacity according to spatial resolution, and Mode-Matched Feature Distillation, which aligns features with a full-fusion teacher. The authors also build Admoab, a 20,000-pair registered infrared-visible benchmark.

entry.title: Contrastive decoding that boosts audio-visual temporal alignment in AI models
entry.summary: Modality-Shift Contrastive Decoding for Temporally Grounded Audio-Visual Understanding arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper finds that audio-visual large language models remain biased toward the originally aligned visual event even when the audio is shifted to overlap a different event, showing limited sensitivity to temporal alignment. The authors propose Modality-Shift Contrastive Decoding (MSCD), a training-free method that contrasts predictions under preserved and disrupted alignment to favor predictions supported by aligned audio and video. Evaluations with two models across three benchmarks show its effectiveness, improving accuracy on Daily-Omni by 2.2 points for OmniVinci and 2.8 points for video-SALMONN 2+.

entry.title: Strategic and Robust Task Allocation for Combat Objectives in Adversarial Multi-Agent Environments
entry.summary: Strategic and Robust Task Allocation for Combat Objectives in Adversarial Multi-Agent Environments arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how a team of agents should assign themselves to contested objectives in games, where decisions must account for uncertainty, space and changing tactics. The authors use a predict-then-optimize approach: a multi-head model predicts tactical signals for each agent, which are combined with rule-based terms into a score matrix, and a minimum-cost flow solver computes global assignments under capacity and stability constraints. Results indicate learned tactical estimates can support stable, feasible and inspectable allocation under real-time limits. The system is an R&D prototype on a commercial game and is not deployed in the shipped game.

entry.title: Equivariant diffusion models for non-abelian lattice gauge theory: theory and scaling tests
entry.summary: Generalizable Equivariant Diffusion Models for Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory: Analytical Foundations and Numerical Scaling Tests arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies gauge-equivariant diffusion models for generating ensembles of field configurations in non-abelian lattice gauge theories. The authors previously showed feasibility by combining L-CNN-based diffusion models with the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA). This work focuses on the analytical framework, deriving the reverse-time stochastic differential equation on the group manifold and discussing gauge invariance of the denoising loss. It also reports numerical benchmarks on scaling with lattice volume and inverse coupling β.

entry.title: OceanFix: Reference-Guided Diffusion for Building 3D Underwater Scenes from Few Views
entry.summary: OceanFix: Reference-Guided Diffusion for Sparse-View Underwater 3D Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents OceanFix, a framework for reconstructing underwater 3D scenes from sparse camera views. It combines diffusion-based view repair with Gaussian splatting scene refinement, using a two-stage training strategy that separates underwater appearance learning from geometric repair. A medium-aware distillation step transfers repaired views into the 3D scene through iterative rendering, repair, and distillation. Experiments on underwater datasets report improved rendering quality, fewer visible artifacts, and finer scene details.

entry.title: High-capacity DAC sorbents that cannot be deployed: pore-filling constraints in multi-objective optimization
entry.summary: When High Capacity Becomes Undeployable: Pore-Filling Constraints for Multi-Objective Optimization of Direct Air Capture Sorbents arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies optimization of amine-impregnated solid sorbents for direct air capture (DAC). The authors add a pore-filling boundary as an explicit constraint to multi-objective Bayesian optimization, using a benchmark of 618 formulations from 43 publications. Unconstrained optimization yields higher nominal capacity but most of its Pareto-optimal candidates violate the pore-filling boundary, while the constrained search shifts toward lower loadings and larger pores. The analysis points to a conservative deployable window at a pore-filling ratio of about 0.4–0.5 (45–55 wt% loading).

entry.title: HSTTA: Label-free adaptation method for matching brain signals to images across people
entry.summary: HSTTA: Hierarchical Selective Test-Time Adaptation for Label-Free Cross-Subject EEG-to-Image Retrieval arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Retrieving images from EEG brain signals performs poorly on new people because of differences between subjects. This paper proposes HSTTA, a hierarchical selective test-time adaptation framework that adapts pretrained models using unlabeled EEG from the target subject. It assigns each query a supervision granularity matching its prediction confidence, and adds two components, CSCC and RHB. On THINGS-EEG2, HSTTA outperforms the strongest EEG-specific test-time adaptation baseline in Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy.

entry.title: Lost in the Grid: Why Multimodal AI Models Fail at Seeing Versus Planning Moves
entry.summary: Lost in the Grid: Where Multimodal LLMs Fail Between Seeing and Planning arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces GridProbe, a diagnostic benchmark that identifies whether multimodal LLMs fail at visual perception, rule application, or multi-step planning in grid games. Tested on Sokoban and a maze game across seven models, it finds that similar success rates hide different bottlenecks, such as planning limits in proprietary models and grid-indexing or rule-application limits in open-source ones. Fine-tuning only the vision module of a perception-limited model on board reading raised its Sokoban success from 5.8% to 20.4% and transferred zero-shot to the maze game. The authors state they will release the benchmark and code.

entry.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Current State
entry.summary: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper compares two ways of handling an agent's context window: harnesses that automatically summarize history when it fills, and models that decide themselves when and what to compact through a context API. Experiments on document research and machine learning engineering tasks covered budgets from 8K to 512K tokens. Models using the API effectively reached higher accuracy, especially at tight budgets, often with fewer input tokens.

entry.title: Non-linear motion from two frames: cubic Hermite paths for video frame interpolation
entry.summary: Non-Linear Motion from Two Frames: Cubic Hermite Trajectories for Video Frame Interpolation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents HermiteVFI, a method for interpolating video frames from two input frames. Instead of linearly resampling endpoint optical flow, it models each pixel's motion as an explicit cubic Hermite trajectory. The measured endpoint displacement fixes the trajectory's positions, while learned endpoint derivatives shape the path between them. Evaluated on X4K1000FPS, SNU-FILM, and Vimeo90K-Septuplet, it shows the largest gains for non-uniform motion and high interpolation ratios.

entry.title: Auto-generating runnable reproducers for AI-reported Linux kernel bugs
entry.summary: Reproducer Synthesis for AI-Reported Bugs in the Linux Kernel arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper introduces ReproCue, a framework that automatically creates runnable proof-of-concept programs for suspected Linux kernel bugs flagged by AI review systems. It replays historical kernel bugs to learn a reproduction state machine for each subsystem, then adjusts the PoC and environment during execution. Across 100 recent AI-generated reviews, it produced PoCs for 49, and Linux kernel maintainers confirmed 69.4% of them.

entry.title: Spe3DUp: Faster image-to-3D generation via faithful trajectory distillation
entry.summary: Spe3DUp: Faithful Trajectory Distillation for Fast Image-to-3D Generation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces Spe3DUp, a coarse-to-fine framework for accelerating image-to-3D mesh generation. Its core method, Faithful Trajectory Distillation (FTD), trains few-step student models to follow the teacher's input-conditioned denoising trajectories, applied separately to coarse geometry generation and geometric refinement. The pipeline is further sped up with efficient geometry decoding and parallel remeshing. Experiments report geometric quality and input correspondence close to the teacher, with 10.0x and 19.9x speedups for the coarse and refinement DiTs and a 7.7x end-to-end speedup.

entry.title: Benefit of Structured Representations: When Equivariance Helps in Image Classification
entry.summary: Benefit of Structured Representations: When Equivariance Helps in Image Classification arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines when vision encoders gain from geometric inductive biases, focusing on the discrete quarter-turn rotation group (C4), which acts without interpolation or boundary artifacts. The authors introduce ConvNeXt-C4, a rotation-equivariant ConvNeXt, which outperforms its base model on all tasks when trained from scratch while using 6x fewer parameters and 1.6x fewer FLOPs. The advantage grows log-linearly as training set size decreases, and the classifier head actively uses retained orientation information, improving performance by 4.90% across datasets.

entry.title: Image detectability field as a viewpoint utility for sparse-map 2D-3D localization
entry.summary: An Image Detectability Field as a Viewpoint Utility for 2D-3D Localization in Sparse Maps arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper asks whether a learned image detectability field can serve as a viewpoint utility for choosing camera views in 2D-3D localization, with the planner reading only map geometry. The field is used without fine-tuning, and a fixed SuperPoint and EPnP-RANSAC localizer estimates pose from the chosen view. Tests on synthetic ShapeNet objects and real SceneFun3D indoor rooms report gains over counting and Harris-3D in sparse maps, and parity with Harris-3D in dense maps.

entry.title: Improving the Delta authorship attribution model with resampling
entry.summary: How resampling method can help us: Improving the Delta model arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Delta is an authorship attribution method based on the most frequent words, and its results are easy to explain in plain English, though its accuracy is not always perfect. This paper proposes applying a resampling method to the selected stylistic features to improve its performance. The results show higher accuracy while the outcomes remain interpretable. The main drawback is the extra computation time needed to obtain more accurate results.

entry.title: SOC-Net: Neural Networks That Enforce Second-Order Cone Constraints
entry.summary: SOC-Net: Second-Order-Cone-Constrained Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 25, 2026SOC-Net is a neural network architecture that enforces input-dependent second-order cone (SOC) constraints by construction for every input, including inputs outside the training distribution. It projects an affine lifting of the backbone output onto the reachable slice of a fixed product of Lorentz cones and maps the correction back to the output space. The authors prove that the network retains the backbone's expressive power under regularity conditions and can be trained end-to-end with standard backpropagation. In experiments on contact force allocation with friction constraints and 3-D obstacle avoidance with an input-robust control barrier function, SOC-Net satisfied the constraints at every evaluated input with lower latency than the solver-based and iterative baselines tested.

entry.title: A protocol for checking whether compressed reference banks still make stable inspection decisions
entry.summary: A Calibration-Referenced Protocol for Measuring Decision Stability under Reference Bank Compression arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents a four-step protocol for measuring how compressing reference banks used in industrial image inspection changes anomaly decisions. Using WideResNet-50 on VisA and MVTec AD, it compares five methods at matched sizes and finds that 10% budget product quantization (PQ) has the lowest decision disagreement, while int8 scalar quantization is lower at the other four budgets. The paper also reports image-level AUROC losses and identifies the evaluation populations most informative for inspection.

entry.title: Agent-as-a-Verifier: Turning Verification Scores into Auditable Evidence
entry.summary: Agent-as-a-Verifier: From Scores to Evidence for General Verification arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces Agent-as-a-Verifier, an agentic system that checks model outputs and produces auditable certificates rather than only scalar scores. Role-separated LLM agents follow a claim-obligation-certificate protocol inspired by formal methods. The authors report higher accuracy than the state-of-the-art approach on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and identify reward-hacking solutions that deceive the benchmark evaluator.

entry.title: Who really wrote the Danish bestseller The Dead Washer? A study using computer text analysis
entry.summary: Is Sara Omar the true author of Dodevaskeren (The Dead Washer)? Authorship attribution in Danish literature arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The 2017 Danish bestseller The Dead Washer was published under the name Sara Omar, but a colleague suggested Mads Peder Nordbo may have written it. Researchers applied four authorship attribution methods, including Delta, intertextual distance, NSC and naive Bayes. Most results matched Nordbo's writing style, but they do not conclusively show he wrote the entire novel. Segment-level analysis found most sections matched Nordbo, while a few passages hint at another unidentified author, possibly Sara Omar herself.

entry.title: WorldPhy: Benchmark for Fine-Grained Physical Realism of Robot World Models
entry.summary: WorldPhy: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Physical Plausibility of World Models in Robotics arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces WorldPhy, a benchmark for evaluating how physically plausible robotics world models are, using 300 tasks spanning varied scenes, task types, viewpoints, and robot setups. The authors collected over 12K human annotations to train WorldPhyReward, a scoring model that rates six fine-grained physical dimensions and instruction following, and that aligns better with human ratings than general VLMs and existing reward models. They evaluated 13 frontier open and closed-source world models. The results show that current models struggle to consistently maintain fine-grained physical plausibility across different robotics scenarios.

entry.title: FoundSurface: A ray-based method that reconstructs 3D scene surfaces from unposed images in one feedforward pass
entry.summary: FoundSurface: Feedforward Ray-Based 3D Scene Surface Reconstruction from Unposed Images arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents a pipeline that recovers continuous, high-fidelity 3D surfaces directly from images without known camera poses, combining pointmap and ray-based representations. It uses a pre-trained pointmap model for geometric priors, selects reference views, and regresses a coarse surface with cross-attention, then refines details with a raylet-based module. The method is trained as one foundation model on 9 datasets and evaluated zero-shot on 6 unseen datasets.

entry.title: Can video AI models guess from partial clues when evidence is incomplete?
entry.summary: Out of Sight, Not Out of Clues: Can Video LLMs Guess from Partial Evidence? arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper introduces ClueProbe, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,721 human-annotated questions over 598 natural videos, labeled as Answerable, Guessable, or Unanswerable, with controlled perturbations to wording or visual input. Evaluating 10 open-source and proprietary Video LLMs, the authors find that failures stem from judgment rather than perception, as models rarely guess from partial clues and instead answer or refuse outright. Targeted fine-tuning that supervises the guess level raises appropriate guessing from 1.6% to 40.4% without extra false refusals.

entry.title: MUSE: Shared Self-Supervised Model with Uncertainty for mmWave Sensing
entry.summary: MUSE: Multi-Task Uncertainty-Aware Self-Supervised Encoder for mmWave ISAC arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes MUSE, a unified framework for millimeter-wave human sensing that replaces separate per-task encoders with one shared self-supervised transformer trained by masked autoencoding across five datasets. During fine-tuning it uses evidential classification heads to quantify uncertainty, enabling selective prediction. The authors report a 9.7 percentage point classification gain over task-specific models and evaluate whether the uncertainty signal stays reliable when deployed on unseen users.

entry.title: Unstable action boundaries in lethal drone AI agents
entry.summary: Unstable Action Boundaries in Lethal Drone Agents arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies whether tool-using large language model agents keep safe action limits when used to control a drone in a military setting. The authors test popular LLMs in a simulated pipeline using real drone imagery, where models must locate requested targets and can call a simulated lethal tool. They report that some agents invoke the lethal tool for generic descriptors such as "people" without any jailbreak. They also find that an agent that seems conservative under protected descriptors can become unsafe after a simple semantic change to the target.

entry.title: From data room to report: AI support for M&A legal due diligence
entry.summary: From Data Room to Report: End-to-End AI Support for M&A Legal Due Diligence arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents LEXI (Legal Extraction and Intelligence), a work-in-progress system that uses large language models to support legal due diligence in mergers and acquisitions. It classifies data room documents, assigns relevant target entities, extracts predefined information with supporting passages and page-level provenance, and prepares report content from reviewed findings. Lawyers review and correct classifications and extractions and remain responsible for legal assessments, recommendations, risk ratings and final wording. Initial evaluations of the classification and extraction components are presented as preliminary evidence of feasibility.

entry.title: A simple, training-free drone agent for finding objects in open environments
entry.summary: A Simple Yet Effective Agent for Open-World Aerial Object Search arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents SimpleUAV, a drone search agent built on a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model that requires no training. It separates judging the target in the current view from choosing actions based on history, and uses local geometry and depth checks to turn visual choices into bounded straight-line moves with execution feedback. The authors report success rates of 41.61% on UAV-ON and 11.98% on AerialDojo-200K, and say the same agent transfers to aerial vision-and-language navigation on TravelUAV.

entry.title: Not every input needs full computation: unifying expert gating, model cascades, and agent orchestration
entry.summary: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This systematic review synthesizes 2,289 studies from 2017 to September 2026 across 20 methodological families, organized under a unified inspect-then-allocate framework for dynamically choosing which experts, models, or agents to invoke. Discrete hard selection accounts for 70%, 83%, and 91% of the token-, query-, and task-scale literature respectively. Computational overhead emerges as a top operational bottleneck across all layers.

entry.title: SysBio-SR: A benchmark testing whether symbolic regression recovers biological reaction mechanisms, not just trajectories
entry.summary: SysBio-SR: Benchmarking Symbolic Regression for Trajectory Fidelity and Mechanism Recovery in Systems Biology arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces SysBio-SR, a benchmark of 198 literature-based biological ODE systems with reaction annotations, including mass action, Michaelis-Menten, Hill, and complex kinetics. It evaluates trajectory fidelity on all systems and mechanism recovery on 161 of them, comparing 11 symbolic-discovery methods. The authors also propose KineSelect, a framework that searches candidate reaction topologies under biological kinetic laws to balance trajectory accuracy with structural parsimony.

entry.title: Learning new visual concepts from one positive and few negative examples
entry.summary: What Makes a Gavagai? Learning Visual Concepts from One Positive and Few Negatives arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces the Gavagai Benchmark, which tests whether vision-language models can identify the visual attributes that define a novel concept using positive and negative examples. The benchmark uses synthetic images with novel combinations of attributes and real images of newly described species. Some models perform poorly even when given correct attributes, while others show large performance gaps when ground-truth attributes are replaced with model predictions, highlighting challenges in both attribute perception and reasoning from limited evidence.

entry.title: Do Machine Learning Ensembles Beat Published Quotas? Target Design and Conformal Intervals Under Admissions Reform
entry.summary: Do Machine Learning Ensembles Beat Published Quotas? Target Parameterization, Censored Baselines, and Conformal Intervals Under Admissions Reform arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper uses audited Vietnamese undergraduate admissions data from 2022 to 2026, covering 309 universities and 26,895 program-year records, to compare machine learning, multilevel, and censored econometric models against published enrollment quotas. Parameterizing the log fill ratio instead of log growth cuts 2024 mean absolute error by 21.5%, and hurdle stacking gives the lowest error. After the 2025 unified-clearing reform, exact quota filling fell to 10.4% and 90% conformal interval coverage dropped from 89.3% to 74.6%.

entry.title: AlignPre: Skill-Aligned Post-Training for Latent-Free Generative Precipitation Nowcasting
entry.summary: AlignPre: Skill-Aligned Post-Training for Latent-Free Generative Precipitation Nowcasting arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents AlignPre, a pixel-space framework for short-term precipitation nowcasting that uses an end-to-end flow-matching forecaster with a hierarchical spatiotemporal architecture and no latent compression. Its post-training method, skill-aligned post-training (SAPT), builds a differentiable objective from the analytic structure of forecast verification scores and backpropagates it to the generator. The authors report that AlignPre outperforms state-of-the-art deterministic and generative baselines in forecast skill across three real-world benchmarks with different forecast horizons.

entry.title: When position misleads left-right part matching in semantic correspondence
entry.summary: When Position Favors the Wrong Part: Evaluating Left-Right Discrimination in Semantic Correspondence arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines whether dense image descriptors can tell apart the correct left or right bilateral part when image position points to the wrong one. The authors compare DINOv2 and MARCO on SPair-71k under agreement and conflict conditions, using odd-component scores and candidate-selection rules. They find that overall accuracy can hide large failures under position conflict.

entry.title: Whose Side Are You On? A Framework and Benchmark for Measuring LLM Political Stances via Politicians' Posts
entry.summary: Whose Side Are You On? A Framework and Benchmark for Assessing LLM Political Stances through Politicians Social Media Posts arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a framework for assessing large language models' political stances through simulated social media interactions, using politicians' posts and multiple prompting methods. The authors build WorldPOLL, a dataset of 4,600 X/Twitter posts from about 200 politicians in ruling and opposition blocs across 23 countries. The analysis examines how support and opposition vary across models, countries, and political directions, and how consistent stances are across prompting methods. It also investigates reasons for disagreement and the effects of model size and instruction tuning on stance inconsistency.
